This exposes a risk of statistically biased inference at reduced precision and provides a further motivation for collecting statistics from ensembles of shorter trajectories.
tldr: The paper analyzes how reduced-precision floating-point arithmetic biases statistical averages in chaotic simulations, using functional graphs and transfer operators to bound errors.
motivation: Reduced-precision arithmetic is increasingly used to speed up scientific simulation and AI hardware, but the authors argue that small arithmetic errors do not guarantee accurate statistics in chaotic systems.
method: They model precision-limited chaotic maps via functional graphs and their transfer operators, deriving bounds on statistical bias and the duration of accurate averaging, and validate with exhaustive numerical experiments on four chaotic maps at 1-24 significand bits including IEEE FP32.
result: Ensembles initially accurate drift toward incorrect statistics as rounding merges trajectories, with lower precision accelerating deterioration; stochastic rounding extends some averaging windows but leaves others severely biased, and longer trajectories can worsen inferred statistics.
conclusion: Reduced precision poses a genuine risk of statistically biased inference, motivating the collection of statistics from ensembles of shorter trajectories rather than single long runs.

title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks For One-Guess Vulnerability Under An Absolute-Moment Budget
authors: Joonas P\"a\"akk\"onen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the average one-guess success probability of an adversary who observes the ordinary integer sum of a finite-support secret and an independent integer-valued mask, subject to an absolute-moment budget on the mask. For a uniform secret on an interval the exact optimum and an explicit optimiser are obtained. For a biased bit the masks that achieve no increase over the prior baseline are characterised and their minimal cost is determined. The entire cost-vulnerability frontier is then determined for every bias. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks. It has infinitely many affine pieces, which accumulate at the critical cost, where the frontier meets the prior baseline with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both the vulnerability and the cost are exactly additive. The results give exact design guidance for additive integer noise under the average one-guess metric; they do not constitute a cryptographic masking scheme.
tldr: This paper derives optimal additive integer masks minimizing average one-guess vulnerability under an absolute-moment cost budget for finite-support secrets.
motivation: The work is motivated by exact design guidance for additive integer noise when an adversary can make a single guess from the observed sum, while the noise is constrained by a moment budget.
method: It uses a layer-cake decomposition of arbitrary masks into shifted truncated geometric masks, along which vulnerability and cost are additive, and solves the optimization exactly for uniform interval secrets and biased bits.
result: For uniform interval secrets the exact optimum and explicit optimizer are given; for biased bits the full cost-vulnerability frontier is characterized as a piecewise-linear interpolation with infinitely many affine pieces accumulating at a critical cost.
conclusion: The results provide exact non-cryptographic design guidance for additive integer noise under average one-guess vulnerability, but the paper explicitly does not propose a cryptographic masking scheme.

title: Rotor-driven Piecewise Cross Polarization Of Wide Quadrupolar Lines: Bath-contact Pumping Of Vector And Tensor Order In Dynamically Polarized Solids
authors: M. F. Hossain D. Keller
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a dynamically polarized solid with a common nuclear spin temperature, spin-1 [MATH]N in ammonia sits at [MATH] when the protons are at [MATH], and a deuteron in a proton-rich matrix at [MATH]. Hartmann--Hahn cross polarization (CP) from the protons could raise either toward [MATH], but the first-order quadrupole interaction spreads the [MATH]N line over [MATH]~MHz at [MATH]~T, far beyond any single contact bandwidth. We develop the theory of CP into one transition of a quadrupolar spin-1, with slow sample rotation carrying each crystallite through a fixed-frequency contact window. A bath contact is an idempotent map on the populations of the contacted transition, so repeated or continuous contacts accumulate rather than cancel, and the hit-once and parity constraints that force stepped rotation for pulsed inversions do not arise. In the small-reservoir limit the population ratio across the contacted transition becomes [MATH], giving [MATH] in one contact and [MATH] in two from [MATH], beyond the unitary bound [MATH]. Under continuous rotation, a window at the Pake horn reaches every bond for an axis perpendicular to the field, while a window in the clean pedestal region, needed for a definite sign of tensor order, reaches a fraction [MATH] at the magic angle [MATH]. Steady-state order is set by the contact rate against rotation-driven cross-branch relaxation, negligible for [MATH]N. In the cubic limit one contact places the spin-1 at the proton temperature ([MATH]), but only a resolved quadrupole splitting permits negative tensor order. The limiting resource is the proton spin lock, which must far exceed the [MATH]~kHz local field for a contact short compared with [MATH], unmeasured at [MATH]~K. Protocols are given for [MATH]N in NH[MATH] and deuterons in NH[MATH]D.
tldr: A theory of Hartmann–Hahn cross polarization into quadrupolar spin-1 nuclei in dynamically polarized solids, combined with slow sample rotation to sweep broadened lines through a fixed contact window.
motivation: Dynamically polarized solids offer large proton polarization, but the first-order quadrupole interaction spreads spin-1 lines (e.g. 14N, deuterons) over MHz, far exceeding any single contact bandwidth, so efficient polarization transfer to these nuclei is thwarted.
method: The authors model cross polarization into a single transition of a quadrupolar spin-1 as an idempotent population map (bath contact), and analyze rotor-driven passage of each crystallite through a fixed-frequency contact window, including cross-branch relaxation and finite proton spin-lock constraints.
result: Repeated contacts accumulate, allowing population ratios beyond the unitary bound in the small-reservoir limit; a Pake-horn window reaches every bond for perpendicular axis, while a pedestal window reaches only a fraction of bonds at the magic angle, and negative tensor order requires resolved quadrupole splitting.
conclusion: The limiting resource is the proton spin lock, which must greatly exceed the kHz local field for short contacts — a quantity unmeasured at the relevant temperatures; protocols are proposed for 14N in NH3 and deuterons in NH3D.

title: High-directivity Pulsed Beams For Effective Power And Information Transfer
authors: Richard W. Ziolkowski
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A vector spherical wave expansion (VSWE) is used to engineer an elemental multipole source whose radiated field is a superdirective, extremely unidirectional (SDEU) needle beam. It is proved analytically and confirmed numerically that the element attains Harrington's normal-directivity value along its beam axis. Its radiated field is linearly polarized with an azimuthally symmetric magnitude; its back lobe vanishes identically in the far field. The unidirectional behavior is quantified at any finite far-field radius by a closed-form front-to-back ratio, obtained from an exact per-degree cancellation of the electric and magnetic multipole contributions in the backward direction. Uniform circular arrays (UCAs) of these elements inherit the SDEU behavior. Driving the arrays with zero-area pulses (ZAPs) transfers the frequency-domain performance intact into the time domain. It is shown that whether the radiated energy beam is narrower or wider than the corresponding intensity beam is decided by a single property of the radiated waveform, not by the size of the radiating aperture. A simple single-cycle ZAP is used to quantify the performance of the UCAs; its energy beam is the narrower one. The same criterion is shown to govern the focal spot of near-field-focused pulse-driven arrays. A custom-designed intensity-enhancement (IE) ZAP is introduced that raises the focal intensity by almost 200-fold over a narrow-band reference while producing a focal spot more than ten times smaller in both the axial and transverse directions, deeply subwavelength with respect to its own effective wavelength. It is demonstrated that these stunning IE results are produced simply with an array of pulse-excited Huygens dipole sources. These results identify the pulse shape, rather than the aperture, as the design variable that governs localized electromagnetic energy and information delivery.
tldr: The paper engineers superdirective, extremely unidirectional electromagnetic needle beams from multipole elements and uniform circular arrays driven by zero-area pulses, showing that pulse shape rather than aperture size governs localized energy and information delivery.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve maximal directivity (Harrington's normal-directivity limit) and tightly localized, deeply subwavelength focal spots for efficient wireless power and information transfer using pulsed excitation.
method: A vector spherical wave expansion is used to design multipole sources with exact per-degree cancellation of electric and magnetic multipole contributions in the backward direction; uniform circular arrays of these elements are driven by zero-area pulses (including a custom intensity-enhancement pulse) and analyzed in the time domain.
result: The element attains Harrington's normal-directivity value with an identically vanishing far-field back lobe and a closed-form front-to-back ratio, arrays inherit the superdirective behavior, and the IE pulse raises focal intensity nearly 200-fold with a focal spot over ten times smaller in axial and transverse directions.
conclusion: Pulse shape, not aperture size, is identified as the design variable controlling beam narrowing and localized electromagnetic energy/information delivery, including for near-field-focused arrays.

title: Hidden Universality Of Rare Fluctuations And A Central-limit Structure At Criticality
authors: Nikolaos G. Fytas, V\'ictor Mart\'in-Mayor, Attilio L. Stella, Gianluca Teza, Alexandros Vasilopoulos, David Yllanes
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The central limit theorem is among the most fundamental principles in the natural sciences, governing the fluctuations of sums of weakly correlated random variables through Gaussian statistics. At critical points, however, long-range correlations invalidate this paradigm, raising a fundamental question: does any general limit theorem survive at criticality? Although scale invariance has long been recognised as the defining feature of typical critical fluctuations, the behaviour of rare fluctuations has remained largely unexplored, as their extraordinarily small probabilities place them beyond the reach of conventional numerical methods. Recent theoretical advances suggest that universal asymptotic laws {may govern large deviations in systems at criticality}, yet direct numerical evidence has been lacking. Here we provide the first such evidence in the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Using large-scale Tethered Monte Carlo simulations, we probe order-parameter fluctuations with probabilities as small as [MATH] and show that, once normalised by their characteristic width, the far tails collapse onto a single asymptotic law shared by distinct microscopic models in the same universality class. This collapse is governed by a universal amplitude, whose numerical extraction is compatible with the conjectured exact result we derive from conformal field theory, and points towards a generalised central limit theorem for critical fluctuations.
tldr: The paper reports numerical evidence for a universal asymptotic law governing rare order-parameter fluctuations at criticality in the 2D Ising universality class.
motivation: The central limit theorem fails at critical points due to long-range correlations, and rare large deviations have remained largely unexplored because their probabilities are extremely small.
method: Large-scale Tethered Monte Carlo simulations are used to probe order-parameter fluctuations with probabilities as small as 10^-100 in the two-dimensional Ising universality class, with theoretical guidance from conformal field theory.
result: After normalization by their characteristic width, far-tail fluctuations collapse onto a single asymptotic law shared by distinct microscopic models in the same universality class, governed by a universal amplitude compatible with a conjectured exact CFT result.
conclusion: The findings point toward a generalized central-limit theorem for critical fluctuations and provide the first direct numerical evidence for universal large-deviation behavior at criticality.

title: Making Poisson {\sigma} Again - An \'etude On Groupoidal Gauging, Anomalies, Gerbes, And Defects
authors: Rafa{\l} R. Suszek
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Poisson [MATH]-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet [MATH] is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle [MATH] with the symplectic structure groupoid [MATH] integrating the Poisson target [MATH], and that of sections of the shadow bundle [MATH] - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of [MATH], modelled on maps from [MATH] into the group of lagrangean bisections of [MATH], which induce Poisson automorphisms of [MATH]. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable [MATH]. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on [MATH] - to a background gerbe over [MATH] endowed with a [MATH]-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows [MATH] of principaloid bundles [MATH] of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack [MATH]. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of [MATH]. The [MATH]-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over [MATH]. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the [MATH]-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of [MATH] - as the datum of the defect.
tldr: The paper reinterprets the Poisson sigma model as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle and generalizes it using gerbes, equivariant structures, and descent to an orbistack.
motivation: It aims to provide a geometric and cohomological understanding of groupoidal gauging, gauge anomalies, and defect structures in the Poisson sigma model.
method: The analysis uses principaloid bundles, symplectic groupoids, gerbes with connection, equivariant structures, and 2-stacky descent to define and generalize the model.
result: The gauge anomaly is derived and shown to vanish for prequantisable targets, and an anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed via coupling to a background gerbe.
conclusion: The generalized Poisson sigma model is formulated as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect, with obstructions to descent discussed cohomologically.

title: Affine Combiners For Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
authors: Alessandro Chiesa, Guy Weissenberg, Eylon Yogev, Kai Zhe Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-[MATH] codes over [MATH], classical scalar combiners achieve error [MATH] in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius. We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words [MATH] as [MATH], where [MATH] are independent uniform elements of [MATH]. For output degree bound [MATH], fixed [MATH] and [MATH], and sufficiently large block length [MATH], we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold [MATH], with error [MATH]. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding. For [MATH], our error is [MATH], an asymptotic factor-[MATH] separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is [MATH] at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error [MATH] when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most [MATH]. We also extend the result to [MATH]-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error [MATH] for fixed [MATH], sufficiently large [MATH], and [MATH], with agreement loss [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves improved Reed-Solomon proximity-gap bounds using affine (two-word) combiners instead of classical scalar combiners, achieving smaller mutual correlated agreement (MCA) error at thresholds approaching the Johnson radius.
motivation: Reed-Solomon proximity gaps underpin the soundness of random-combination-based testing in proof systems, and classical scalar combiners give suboptimal error bounds, especially beyond unique decoding near the Johnson radius.
method: The authors analyze affine combiners that mix two received words with independent uniform field elements, and prove MCA guarantees with at most one coordinate of agreement loss over arbitrary evaluation domains in any finite field; they also establish matching worst-case lower bounds for scalar combiners and for affine combiners without agreement loss, and extend the analysis to multivariate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids.
result: For output degree bound, fixed rate and sufficiently large block length, they obtain MCA error with a factor-separation improvement over scalar combiners (asymptotically a factor of about q), show that one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for their guarantee, and extend the results to Reed-Muller codes.
conclusion: Affine combiners yield strictly better proximity-gap error bounds than scalar combiners, with the small agreement-loss relaxation being both necessary and cheap, advancing the theory of coding-based proof systems.

title: Duft: Device-Unique Feedback Traversal For Entropy-Estimated Response Extraction And Mutual Authentication Using Sram PUFs
authors: Syed Talha Imam, Amna Zafar, Arslan Munir
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) are a promising technology in the realm of random number generation for key generation, but for PUF-based authentication, they have been sidelined due to their limited challenge space as a reservoir of Challenge-Response Pairs (CRPs). In this paper, we develop a seed-based, round-iterated feedback mechanism, which we name Device-Unique Feedback Traversal (DUFT). The feedback chain is driven by the device's unstable and stable bit positions in its stability mask against the address to create a unique traversal. Additionally, a device-key hashed from the unique SRAM-PUF array is also included in calculating the next round of the chain to keep it secret. By estimating the physical SRAM source's entropy and error rate empirically, or by having a source with established metrics in both, DUFT estimates the number of rounds of feedback in the traversal to be performed to achieve a certain amount of min-entropy. We reach 128 bits of estimated min-entropy on our reference hardware under stated assumptions and experimental estimates. The number of rounds in the traversal scales directly with measured source-entropy, allowing security to be increased for weaker sources at the cost of running time. Using this feedback-traversal wrapper over SRAM-PUFs to obtain a measured-response, we propose an extremely lightweight authentication and key-encapsulation protocol for resource-constrained embedded devices. We realize and evaluate DUFT end-to-end on physical IoT/embedded hardware: a discrete-SRAM node pair running the complete mechanism and end-to-end protocol, and an embedded-SRAM microcontroller for the mechanism alone.
tldr: The paper proposes DUFT, a device-unique feedback traversal mechanism over SRAM PUFs for entropy-estimated response extraction, mutual authentication, and lightweight key encapsulation on embedded/IoT devices.
motivation: SRAM PUFs are useful for key generation but have limited challenge-response pair space, limiting their use in PUF-based authentication.
method: DUFT uses stable and unstable SRAM bit positions in a stability mask to drive a seed-based, round-iterated feedback traversal, incorporates a device-key hash, and estimates the number of rounds needed to reach a target min-entropy.
result: The authors achieve 128 bits of estimated min-entropy on reference hardware and demonstrate end-to-end authentication/key encapsulation on discrete-SRAM IoT nodes and an embedded-SRAM microcontroller.
conclusion: DUFT provides a lightweight, entropy-scalable authentication wrapper for resource-constrained devices using SRAM PUFs, though it is a classical hardware-security contribution rather than a quantum information result.

title: Quantitative Gaussian Limits Of Periodic O(n) Models At And Below The Critical Temperature
authors: Weiqi Jiang, Pengcheng Hou, Zhiyi Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a volume-uniform Gaussian approximation for local spin coordinates in the zero-field nearest-neighbour [MATH] model on periodic boxes of side [MATH] in [MATH], at and below the critical temperature of the limiting spherical model. On a fixed spatial window, for sufficiently large [MATH], the unnormalized [MATH]-Wasserstein error for the first [MATH] coordinates is at most [MATH], where [MATH] is the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model. The estimate is uniform on compact ranges of positive directional couplings and inverse temperatures. The target has independent coordinate fields, each a scaled anisotropic Gaussian free field with an independent spatially constant Gaussian term below criticality. On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its [MATH] positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as [MATH] exactly when [MATH] and [MATH]. For any choice of periodic infinite-volume accumulation states, the error on any nonempty fixed window tends to zero as [MATH] exactly when [MATH]. In [MATH], when the inverse temperature exceeds its critical value by at least a fixed positive amount, the bound improves to [MATH]. For fixed [MATH], the sharp order is [MATH] on star-containing windows and [MATH] on every nonempty fixed window in periodic accumulation states.
tldr: The paper proves volume-uniform Gaussian approximation bounds for local spin coordinates in periodic O(n) models at and below the spherical-model critical temperature.
motivation: It aims to quantitatively characterize critical fluctuations of O(n) spin models by comparing finite-volume local coordinates to Gaussian limits with sharp Wasserstein error rates.
method: The authors establish Gaussian approximation estimates for local spin coordinates on periodic boxes, using the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model and analyzing Wasserstein distance on fixed spatial windows.
result: They obtain error bounds that are uniform over compact parameter ranges, identify sharp orders on star-containing windows and general fixed windows, and improve the bound in d=3 sufficiently below criticality.
conclusion: The work provides precise Gaussian fluctuation limits for periodic O(n) models, but it is a mathematical statistical-mechanics result rather than a quantum-information or information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Rational Layers In The Low Temperature Expansion Of The Three-dimensional Ising Model
authors: Ran Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A low-temperature expansion orders Ising droplets by wall area, but droplets with different transverse spans can occur at the same order. We instead organize the zero-field simple-cubic model by the excess above the minimum wall area compatible with two prescribed spans. We prove that every fixed excess layer, including all logarithmic cover corrections and Euler inversion, has a rational bivariate generating function with denominator factors restricted to 1 - x, 1 - y and 1 - x - y. The proof compresses repeated coordinate cuts into bounded decorations and assigns each unbounded interval to one monotone chain. A finite controller then enforces induced contacts and arbitrary cover-color reuse. We explicitly assemble the complete layers of excess zero through three over all widths, attributing their known geometric constituents to earlier polyomino enumeration. Exact lattice checks corroborate the formulas. A certified low-temperature comparison shows a modest hybrid accuracy gain at one sampling point and higher evaluation cost. The result establishes an exact layer structure; summation over unbounded excess remains a separate problem.
tldr: The paper proves that fixed-excess layers in the low-temperature expansion of the simple-cubic Ising model have rational bivariate generating functions and explicitly computes layers of excess zero through three.
motivation: Low-temperature expansions organize Ising droplets by wall area, but droplets with different transverse spans can appear at the same order, motivating a refined organization by excess above the minimum compatible wall area.
method: The author compresses repeated coordinate cuts into bounded decorations, assigns unbounded intervals to monotone chains, and uses a finite controller to enforce induced contacts and cover-color reuse.
result: Every fixed excess layer, including logarithmic cover corrections and Euler inversion, is shown to have a rational bivariate generating function with denominator factors restricted to 1-x, 1-y, and 1-x-y; explicit layers for excess zero through three are assembled and checked against exact lattice computations.
conclusion: The work establishes an exact layer structure for the low-temperature expansion, though summation over unbounded excess remains open and the practical accuracy gain is modest at higher evaluation cost.

title: Distilling An Atomistic Foundation Model Is All You Need For Large-scale Molecular Dynamics Of Semiconductor Interfaces
authors: Feiyu Zhou, Wei Qiu, Fei Shuang, Yilun Liu, Shengying Yue, Penghua Ying
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. From 128 pretrained models spanning 22 model families, we select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher and train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning, with both simulation speed and accessible system size improved by several orders of magnitude relative to the teacher model. Matched training configurations and architectures enable direct comparisons with students trained on density-functional-theory (DFT) reference labels. For 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces, direct distillation preserves termination-dependent thermal conductance and dominant spectral features, with conductance differing by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts. In 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens loaded at 500 K, tensile strength and loading work differ by 2.8% and 1.5%, respectively. Exploratory SiC/a-C/SiC simulations retain the principal thermal bottleneck and the direction of the annealing response. Furthermore, a four-model committee retrieves 42-56% of the highest-error teacher configurations with a 10% selection budget and improves high-error force fitting, but does not consistently improve downstream properties. These findings demonstrate that direct distillation can preserve key interfacial thermal and mechanical responses in compact interatomic potentials, opening a path towards large-scale, high-throughput simulations of heterogeneous interfaces.
tldr: The paper distills a pretrained atomistic foundation model into compact ACE and NEP interatomic potentials to enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces while preserving key thermal and mechanical responses.
motivation: Atomistic foundation models offer transferable energy and force predictions but are too computationally expensive for large-scale molecular dynamics, motivating distillation into fast compact potentials for interface simulations.
method: The authors select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher from 128 pretrained models and train ACE and NEP student potentials via direct distillation, comparing them against students trained on DFT labels in large BAs/GaN, Cu/diamond, and SiC/a-C/SiC systems.
result: Direct distillation preserves termination-dependent thermal conductance within 6.6% of DFT-trained counterparts in 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces and keeps tensile strength and loading work within 2.8% and 1.5% in Cu/diamond, while a four-model committee only partially improves high-error force fitting.
conclusion: Direct distillation can retain important interfacial thermal and mechanical responses in compact potentials, enabling large-scale high-throughput molecular dynamics of heterogeneous interfaces, though committee-based active learning does not consistently improve downstream properties.

title: Analytic T-Matrix Formalism For Helmholtz Resonators
authors: Egor V. Domoratskii, Polina A. Medvedeva, Dmitrii N. Maksimov, Lana A. Glazko, Alexey A. Proskurin, Nikolay S. Solodovchenko, Mingzhao Song, Yong Li, Mihail I. Petrov, Andrey A. Bogdanov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an analytic T-matrix formalism for two-dimensional circular acoustic Helmholtz resonators with thin rigid walls. The central idea is to use an aperture projection operator to obtain a compact expression for the T-matrix with explicit coefficients describing coupling and decoupling between external fields and cavity resonances. An equivalent formulation providing much faster convergence uses an aperture-to-Fourier map and an edge-adapted basis for the aperture flux. The method extends directly to multiple apertures of arbitrary angular widths and positions. The calculated scattering spectra agree with full-wave numerical simulations. For single- and double-aperture resonators, we decompose the T-matrix into even and odd parts under inversion to identify the channels associated with Willis coupling. We show how internal losses enable direction-dependent scattering and absorption when inversion symmetry is broken, while reciprocity ensures equal extinction for opposite incidence. Finally, we show how shifting the expansion origin redistributes radiation among multipole channels, enabling more compact T-matrix representations.
tldr: The paper develops an analytic T-matrix formalism for acoustic Helmholtz resonators with thin rigid walls and multiple apertures.
motivation: Accurate and compact modeling of acoustic resonator scattering is needed to describe coupling between external fields and cavity resonances, including effects such as Willis coupling.
method: The authors introduce an aperture projection operator to derive a compact T-matrix, plus an equivalent aperture-to-Fourier map and edge-adapted basis for faster convergence, and decompose the T-matrix into even and odd parts under inversion.
result: Calculated scattering spectra agree with full-wave simulations, and the formalism reveals direction-dependent scattering and absorption from internal losses when inversion symmetry is broken while reciprocity ensures equal extinction for opposite incidence.
conclusion: The analytic T-matrix approach provides a compact and interpretable framework for acoustic Helmholtz resonator scattering and multipole channel analysis.

title: Exact Output Steering With Vanishing Controls In Weighted Shift Dynamics
authors: Yunied Puig
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls. For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.
tldr: The paper characterizes exact output steering with vanishing controls in wrapped weighted shift dynamics and residual shifts, with applications to structured machine-learning representations.
motivation: The work aims to understand controllability and steering in weighted shift dynamical systems when control inputs vanish, using spectral and arithmetic conditions.
method: It analyzes wrapped weighted shifts, residualizations, expansive cycle multipliers, residue separation, spectral-toral mechanisms, conjugate planes, and orbit dictionaries.
result: Steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier plus a residue condition for wrapped shifts, and by radial expansion with an arithmetic parity condition for residual shifts, yielding bounded-gap steering times and control estimates.
conclusion: The paper provides exact steering criteria for weighted shift dynamics and derives a two-scale gain condition for machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries.

title: Robust High-Order Bug Integrators Without Basis Augmentation
authors: Shiheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop robust high-order basis-update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation without basis augmentation or rank truncation. The basis and core updates use the same approximate increment. We establish a two-sided relaxed-exactness estimate that controls the error in the low-rank approximation by the increment error. Under the stated assumptions on the vector field and its normal component, sufficiently accurate increments yield local and global error bounds whose constants and step-size restrictions are independent of small singular values. Using explicit Runge--Kutta increments, we obtain robust orders two, three, and four for the explicit midpoint method, Heun's third-order method, and Merson's fourth-order method, respectively. Every internal stage and final approximation has rank at most the prescribed rank [MATH]. We also prove that these orders are retained under arbitrary basis augmentation followed by best rank-[MATH] SVD truncation at the internal stages and the endpoint, without a separate assumption on the truncation error. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence orders and show comparable performance with and without augmentation.
tldr: The paper develops robust high-order basis-update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation that avoid basis augmentation and rank truncation while retaining provable convergence orders two through four.
motivation: High-order low-rank integrators typically require basis augmentation and truncation steps whose interplay with error control is poorly understood, especially when singular values become small and standard error constants blow up.
method: The authors use a single approximate increment for both basis and core updates and prove a two-sided relaxed-exactness estimate bounding the low-rank approximation error by the increment error; explicit Runge-Kutta increments (midpoint, Heun, Merson) are then analyzed, including the case of arbitrary basis augmentation followed by best rank-r SVD truncation.
result: Local and global error bounds with constants and step-size restrictions independent of small singular values are established, yielding robust orders two, three, and four, with every internal stage and final approximation of rank at most r; numerics confirm the predicted orders and comparable performance with and without augmentation.
conclusion: Augmentation-free BUG integrators can be made robustly high-order for dynamical low-rank approximation, removing the need for separate truncation-error assumptions.

title: Incrementally Verifiable Oracle Aided Computation
authors: Yael Kalai Shafi Goldwasser
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incrementally verifiable computation (IVC) allows a prover to maintain a short proof that can be efficiently updated after each computation step, without retaining or recomputing the preceding execution. Standard IVC schemes do not directly address a crucial feature of AI tasks: their dependence on external information and expertise. We construct IVC schemes for oracle-aided computations under the LWE assumption by first constructing SNARGs, and then extending them to IVC. We consider the following two settings, where below, k is the security parameter, n is the input length, and T, S, and Q are the time, space, and oracle-query bounds. 1. Robust computations: For bounded-space computations, including non-deterministic computations, in which every accepting purported execution on a false input contains at least an eps-fraction of incorrect oracle answers, we construct privately verifiable SNARGs and IVC. Public parameters, private verification keys, and proofs have length poly(k ,S, log T,1/eps), and verification uses O(k/eps) oracle calls. We complement this result with a lower bound ruling out (deterministic) publicly verifiable SNARGs and IVCs with public parameters of length o(n), and o(Q) verifier oracle queries. 2. Signed oracles: For oracles that digitally sign their query-answer pairs, we construct publicly verifiable SNARGs and IVC without a robustness assumption, and with oracle-free setup and verification. Public parameters and proofs have length poly(k,S,log T). For deterministic computations with oracle query and answer lengths poly(k,log T), we remove the dependence on S, obtaining public parameter and proof lengths poly(k,log T). All our constructions have adaptive completeness and soundness.
tldr: The paper constructs incrementally verifiable computation (IVC) schemes for oracle-aided computations under the LWE assumption, via privately/publicly verifiable SNARGs, for robust bounded-space computations and for signed oracles.
motivation: Standard IVC only certifies a prover's own computation steps and does not handle AI-style tasks that depend on external oracles providing information and expertise; the authors therefore extend IVC to oracle-aided settings.
method: They first build SNARGs for oracle-aided computations from LWE, then lift them to IVC, treating two models: robust computations where any false accepted execution must contain an ε-fraction of wrong oracle answers, and signed oracles that authenticate query-answer pairs; a lower bound rules out short-parameter publicly verifiable schemes in the robust setting.
result: For robust bounded-space computation they obtain privately verifiable SNARGs/IVC with poly(k,S,log T,1/ε) parameters and O(k/ε) verifier oracle calls; for signed oracles they get publicly verifiable, oracle-free-setup SNARGs/IVC with poly(k,S,log T) parameters, and for deterministic computations with poly(k,log T)-length queries/answers the S-dependence is removed.
conclusion: Oracle-aided IVC is achievable under LWE with adaptive completeness and soundness, giving succinct verifiable delegation of computations that consult external information sources, with matching impossibility results in the robust public-verification regime.

title: Bayesian Inference With A Polymer Probabilistic Computer
authors: Travis Wanless, Yuriy Bandera, Lubomir Kostal, Stephen H. Foulger
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian inference weighs competing explanations of noisy data by sampling from a posterior distribution, a task that deterministic hardware performs only by simulating randomness. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) supply this randomness physically, but the few hardware networks of p-bits built so far use inorganic devices, address optimization or learning, and are judged without reference to the spread expected from finite sampling. Here we report a probabilistic computer built from solution-processed conjugated-polymer memristors. Four polymer p-bits, tracked online for drift and coupled in a closed Gibbs-sampling loop, sample competing, degenerate and cooperative posteriors over sixteen states with statistics that fall within the range of ideal p-bits, both in their distribution and in their autocorrelation, without any parameter fitted to the target. This agreement extends to new simulated sensor readings whose outcome was predicted before each run, including readings that point away from the true answer. Reprogrammed in software, the same circuit and controller reproduces the invertible AND gate of earlier p-bit networks, with its temperature fixed in advance rather than fitted. Polymer p-bits thus open a route to printed, large-area probabilistic computers that infer alongside their sensors.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a classical probabilistic computer built from conjugated-polymer memristor p-bits for Bayesian inference via Gibbs sampling.
motivation: Bayesian inference requires sampling from posterior distributions, and physical p-bits can provide randomness without deterministic simulation, but existing p-bit hardware is mostly inorganic and not assessed against finite-sampling statistics.
method: Four solution-processed polymer memristor p-bits are tracked online for drift and coupled in a closed Gibbs-sampling loop to sample posterior distributions over sixteen states; the same circuit is reprogrammed in software for an invertible AND gate.
result: The polymer p-bit network samples degenerate and cooperative posteriors with distributions and autocorrelations consistent with ideal p-bits, and it predicts new simulated sensor outcomes without target-fitted parameters.
conclusion: Polymer p-bits offer a route toward printed, large-area probabilistic computers that can perform inference alongside sensors, but the work is classical probabilistic hardware rather than quantum information science.

title: A Multi-Prover Interactive Protocol For Certification Of Resolution Refutations
authors: Philipp Czerner, Adrian Krauss, Josia Pietsch, Javier Esparza
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A resolution refutation of a SAT-formula [MATH] is an independently checkable certificate proving that [MATH] is unsatisfiable. However, the refutations of [MATH] can be exponentially larger than [MATH]. So, a verifier needs worst-case exponential time in the size of [MATH] to check their correctness. We present ResCertify, an interactive probabilistic protocol in which the verifier interacts with multiple independent, untrusted provers (MIP) to check the refutation with very low probability of error. The verifier runs in linear time in the size of [MATH]. The provers require time [MATH], where [MATH] is the resolution refutation and [MATH] is the number of variables of [MATH]. If they can be trusted to act as a multilinear oracle on certain queries, a single prover suffices, and the runtime can be improved to [MATH]. Finally, while the focus of our work is theoretical, we also report on a proof-of-concept implementation of ResCertify.
tldr: The paper introduces ResCertify, a multi-prover interactive protocol for certifying resolution refutations of unsatisfiable SAT formulas in verifier time linear in the formula size.
motivation: Resolution refutations can be exponentially larger than the original SAT formula, forcing a verifier to spend exponential time checking correctness directly.
method: The authors design an interactive probabilistic protocol in which a verifier interacts with multiple independent untrusted provers, using a multilinear-oracle variant for a single-prover setting.
result: The verifier runs in linear time in the formula size, while the provers require time polynomial in the refutation size and number of variables; a proof-of-concept implementation is also reported.
conclusion: ResCertify provides an efficient interactive certification scheme for resolution refutations, but it is a classical complexity/proof-checking result with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems contribution.

title: The Price Of Anarchy In Markets For Lemons
authors: Tim Roughgarden Naveen Durvasula
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the worst-case equilibrium gains from trade in simple bilateral trade mechanisms with interdependent valuations. Equilibria in such settings are typically complex, as proposed prices can convey private information held by the proposer. Such equilibria suffer lost gains from trade both due to the inefficiency introduced by screening (as in independent private value settings) and due to adverse selection. We identify broad conditions under which, nevertheless, sequential equilibria are guaranteed to achieve a constant fraction of the first-best gains from trade. Our bounds quantify the central role of rare pessimistic seller signals and rare optimistic buyer signals. The results apply to seller-proposer, buyer-proposer, and random-proposer mechanisms. The key idea in our analysis is to relate equilibrium gains from trade to proposer profits in an auxiliary market with independent private values.
tldr: This paper studies worst-case equilibrium gains from trade in simple bilateral trade mechanisms with interdependent valuations and adverse selection.
motivation: The authors aim to understand when sequential equilibria can still guarantee a constant fraction of first-best gains from trade despite screening inefficiencies and adverse selection.
method: They analyze seller-proposer, buyer-proposer, and random-proposer mechanisms, relating equilibrium gains from trade to proposer profits in an auxiliary independent-private-values market.
result: They identify broad conditions under which sequential equilibria achieve a constant fraction of first-best gains from trade, with bounds highlighting rare pessimistic seller signals and rare optimistic buyer signals.
conclusion: The work quantifies the price of anarchy in lemons markets and clarifies how interdependent valuations and signaling affect equilibrium efficiency.

title: VRMaaS: Verifiable Reward-Model-as-a-Service For Trustworthy Llm Alignment
authors: Guofu Liao, Hailang Xi, Taotao Wang, Shengli Zhang, Rongcheng Tu, Hao Liao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reward models (RMs) are increasingly deployed as service components in LLM alignment pipelines, where payment, audit, moderation, and governance workflows act on the scores they return. An inference proof alone does not show whether a score belongs to the intended request, model checkpoint, numerical configuration, and verifier: in a controlled comparison that isolates the accepted statement from prover scale, a generic inference proof wrapped for on-chain checking remains valid after six classes of such service-field substitution. We formulate verifiable reward-model-as-a-service (VRMaaS) as a service-output integrity problem and present a framework in which each returned reward becomes a proof-carrying artifact. Its off-chain acceptance rule binds request identity, committed weights, verifier and configuration identifiers, proof-task order, and the digest of the exported package, so auditors can check a reward without rerunning the private RM or exposing inputs, checkpoints, or hidden activations; an optional on-chain zero-knowledge wrapper gives contracts a partial attestation of selected consistency checks and supplied service fields. The framework decomposes Transformer RM serving into arithmetic and lookup-backed proof tasks, aggregates them into a composite proof, and links hidden operands to the committed weights. A GPU prototype on 1B, 3B, and 8B reward models over 128-1024 tokens preserves 93.5-99% pairwise agreement with the baseline RM and rejects every tested service-field substitution in complete artifacts. Using exact integer witnesses and request-level aggregation of weight-binding openings, it generates complete artifacts in 49.8-206.1 seconds across the evaluated settings; auditors verify retained artifacts in 1.94-5.11 seconds, and partial public attestation costs about 217K gas. These costs suit delayed audit, settlement, and governance workflows.
tldr: VRMaaS turns each reward-model score in an LLM alignment pipeline into a proof-carrying artifact, binding request identity, committed weights, verifier and configuration fields, and package digest so auditors can verify rewards without rerunning the private model.
motivation: Inference proofs alone do not guarantee that a returned reward corresponds to the intended request, model checkpoint, numerical configuration, and verifier; generic proofs remain valid under six classes of service-field substitution, creating an integrity gap in paid, audited, or governed RM services.
method: The framework decomposes Transformer reward-model serving into arithmetic and lookup-backed proof tasks, aggregates them into a composite proof linked to committed weights, and optionally wraps selected consistency checks in an on-chain zero-knowledge attestation, using exact integer witnesses and request-level aggregation of weight-binding openings.
result: A GPU prototype on 1B, 3B, and 8B reward models over 128-1024 tokens preserves 93.5-99% pairwise agreement with the baseline RM, rejects all tested service-field substitutions, generates artifacts in 49.8-206.1 s, verifies them in 1.94-5.11 s, and costs about 217K gas for partial public attestation.
conclusion: Proof-carrying reward outputs provide a practical service-output integrity guarantee for LLM alignment pipelines, with costs compatible with delayed audit, settlement, and governance workflows.

title: Multimodal Semantic Communication Using Shared And Unique Representation Decomposition
authors: Ying-Chang Liang Peng Yi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.
tldr: A multimodal semantic communication framework that splits learned representations into shared and modality-specific parts, transmitting shared components as codebook indices and unique components in analog form.
motivation: Semantic communication promises bandwidth savings for mobile and vehicular networks, but heterogeneous modalities create a semantic representation gap when one modality carries information not inferable from the other.
method: The authors formulate a mutual-information objective combining source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of shared components, and decoupling of shared versus modality-specific features, with a learned compact codebook for digital transmission of shared features and knowledge distillation from a pretrained vision foundation model.
result: On image-text pairs over AWGN and EVA channels, the framework improves image reconstruction relative to separate source-channel coding and representative multimodal/unimodal SemCom baselines, with graceful degradation under channel-estimation mismatch.
conclusion: Decomposing shared and unique semantic components with a shared codebook yields efficient multimodal semantic transmission, though the work is a classical deep-learning communication scheme with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection For Embedded Hypercubes And Beta--Gaussian Mixtures
authors: Ali Darijani, Emadedin Soufian, J\"urgen Beyerer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive closed-form Gaussian information projections of Beta--Gaussian distributions whose tangential components are supported on affine embedded hypercubes and whose normal components are Gaussian. The optimal Gaussian is uniquely characterized by moment matching, and the corresponding minimum Kullback--Leibler divergence admits an explicit expression depending only on the intrinsic Beta parameters, independently of the embedding geometry, ambient dimension, and normal Gaussian parameters. In the uniform case, this divergence reduces to a linear function of the intrinsic dimension. We further extend this construction to finite, pure embedded cubical complexes by considering mixtures of the componentwise Gaussian projections. Using the joint convexity of the Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish an explicit upper bound on the approximation error of the resulting Gaussian Mixture. For uniform tangential distributions and volume-based mixture weights, the bound is linear in the intrinsic dimension and independent of the geometry of the complex, its embedding, and the normal Gaussian parameters.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form Gaussian information projections for Beta--Gaussian distributions supported on embedded hypercubes and extends the result to mixtures via cubical complexes.
motivation: Gaussian information projection and KL-divergence bounds are useful for approximating structured distributions, but closed-form expressions for Beta--Gaussian models on embedded cubical supports are not generally available.
method: The authors characterize the optimal Gaussian by moment matching, derive an explicit minimum KL divergence depending only on intrinsic Beta parameters, and bound mixture approximation error using joint convexity of KL divergence.
result: The minimum KL divergence is independent of embedding geometry, ambient dimension, and normal Gaussian parameters; for uniform tangential distributions and volume-based mixture weights, the error bound is linear in intrinsic dimension.
conclusion: The work provides analytic projection formulas and approximation guarantees for Beta--Gaussian and cubical-complex mixture models, but it is a classical statistics/information-geometry contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems content.

title: Privacy Leakage From Recurrent State In Llm Inference
authors: Weimin Fu, Shikun Liu, Qiying Li, Yuntao Liu, Pan Li, Xiaolong Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personalized LLM services place private facts and application instructions into a prompt, then retain representations of that context for later inference. Latent-state LLMs compress part of this history into fixed-size recurrent state. The information preserved by its learned updates is implicit, and later computation can expose it even when an observer receives neither the private text nor the responses. We investigate privacy leakage from recurrent state through partial-state probing and physical observation of its use. Our methodology separates recoverable information, persistence through public dialogue, causal influence on later decisions, and leakage through power. Experiments with released hybrid implementations show that a small state observation supports multiple predictions about private facts and response rules, and that personal attributes generalize to unseen authors. The information remains inferable after public dialogue and changes later decision margins. Complete-read power recovers private facts under a fixed execution schedule. On a partitioned GPU, an unprivileged account infers age from whole-device power during public requests; a separate state-isolation experiment establishes the recurrent contribution to this channel. These findings extend context confidentiality to the lifetime and execution of retained state. They identify access-control responsibilities for serving systems, telemetry restrictions for GPU operators, and data-dependent power leakage for accelerator designers.
tldr: The paper shows that the fixed-size recurrent state of latent-state LLMs leaks private prompt information, recoverable via partial-state probing, persistence across public dialogue, and even whole-device GPU power measurements.
motivation: Personalized LLM services store private facts and instructions in internal representations, and the authors ask whether compressed recurrent state retains information that later computation can expose to observers who never see the text or outputs.
method: They perform partial-state probing to separate recoverable information, persistence, and causal influence on later decisions, plus a complete-read power analysis under fixed execution schedules and a state-isolation experiment on a partitioned GPU with an unprivileged account.
result: Small state observations support multiple predictions about private facts and response rules, generalize to unseen authors, survive public dialogue, shift decision margins, and allow age inference from whole-device power; the isolation experiment confirms the recurrent state's contribution to the power channel.
conclusion: Context confidentiality must extend to the lifetime and execution of retained state, implying access-control duties for serving systems, telemetry restrictions for GPU operators, and data-dependent power leakage concerns for accelerator designers.

title: The Ultimate Karp-Lipton Collapse
authors: Ilya Volkovich Edward A. Hirsch (ariel University)
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Karp and Lipton proved that if [MATH], then [MATH] collapses. A long line of work pushed the collapse to smaller classes. In particular, Chakaravarthy and Roy obtained two such collapses, to (apparently) incomparable classes [MATH] and [MATH]. We united them earlier by a collapse to the input-oblivious version [MATH] of [MATH], which is contained in both; and, jointly with Williams, to a slightly smaller class. Two other deepest known collapses are to [MATH] (following from K\"obler and Watanabe) and to [MATH] (proved in this paper). We unite the three collapses by a collapse to a class contained in all of them. We use a three-stage computational model OGTD (oblivious generator-tester-decoder): a polynomial-time generator with an oracle computes an advice string from [MATH], a tester certifies it, and a polynomial-time decoder uses it (it is the only one that sees the actual input). Let [MATH] be the class of OGTD languages defined by a restricted version of [MATH] as the generator's oracle, by a co-[MATH] tester, and a [MATH] decoder. We show that it is contained in the three collapse classes above and prove that [MATH] collapses to [MATH] under [MATH]. The collapse also holds for an unambiguous version of [MATH]. All these input-oblivious collapse classes lie in [MATH], and so do even the non-input-oblivious versions [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH]: we prove that [MATH]. This strengthens the containment [MATH] of Chakaravarthy and Roy and our earlier containment [MATH]. The proof unites the Goldreich-Wigderson-type procedure of Chakaravarthy and Roy with our earlier approximate-counting technique. Its input-oblivious counterpart concerns [MATH], the first collapse class of Chakaravarthy and Roy: every language in [MATH] has polynomial-size circuits constructible in [MATH].
tldr: The paper unifies several known Karp-Lipton-style collapses of the polynomial hierarchy under the assumption NP ⊆ P/poly into a single collapse to an input-oblivious complexity class defined via a three-stage generator-tester-decoder model.
motivation: A long line of work has progressively pushed the Karp-Lipton collapse to smaller complexity classes, yielding several apparently incomparable collapse classes; the authors aim to unify these results under one contained class.
method: They introduce the OGTD (oblivious generator-tester-decoder) computational model with a polynomial-time generator using a restricted oracle, a co-NP tester, and a P/poly decoder, and combine a Goldreich-Wigderson-type procedure with an approximate-counting technique.
result: The new class is shown to be contained in the three deepest known collapse classes, the collapse holds for an unambiguous variant, and the containment results are strengthened to show the relevant classes lie in a common class.
conclusion: The work provides the 'ultimate' unifying Karp-Lipton collapse, subsuming prior incomparable collapses and strengthening containments among non-input-oblivious classes.

title: Hopf Algebras Of Leaf-graded Forests
authors: Elizabeth Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.
tldr: The paper relates a Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests to Bruned's Hopf algebra from stochastic-PDE renormalization, showing duality with pre-Lie insertion Hopf algebras graded by leaf number.
motivation: Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue (studied by Foissy via twisted combinatorial bialgebras) underlie renormalization of stochastic PDEs; the author seeks to connect these structures to her own leaf-graded Hopf algebra on binary forests.
method: Combinatorial and algebraic: constructs pre-Lie insertion operations that respect leaf count, establishes duality between the resulting Hopf algebras and Bruned's (and its reduced form), computes Hochschild 1-cocycles, and proves a universal property.
result: Bruned's Hopf algebra is shown to be dual to a leaf-graded Hopf algebra from leaf-preserving pre-Lie insertions, satisfies an analogue of the Connes-Kreimer universal property, and admits explicit Hochschild 1-cocycles.
conclusion: The work unifies several Hopf-algebraic structures arising in stochastic-PDE renormalization, placing Bruned's algebra within a broader Connes-Kreimer-type framework via leaf gradings.

title: Relative-energy Stabilization Of An Irreversible port-Hamiltonian Tubular Reactor
authors: Weijun. Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a relative-energy control approach for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular reactor around a spatially nonuniform stationary profile. The starting point is a thermodynamic duality between the entropy-based availability used in earlier reactor control and the relative Hamiltonian induced by the irreversible port-Hamiltonian representation. Under physically interpretable stability conditions---positive heat capacity, positive compressibility and positive compositional susceptibility---the Hamiltonian density is shown to be strictly convex, while the corresponding entropy representation is strictly concave. The resulting relative Hamiltonian decomposes into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing contributions and yields an exact relative-energy balance in which irreversible dissipation is separated from profile-dependent terms. This structure leads to a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback that injects thermal damping without cancelling the nonlinear PDE dynamics. A continuous coercivity condition gives a local a-priori decay estimate for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions, while a composite energy functional provides an exponential estimate for the linearized closed-loop initial-boundary value problem. Structure-preserving PFEM simulations are used to verify the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.
tldr: The paper develops a relative-energy (relative-Hamiltonian) control design for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular chemical reactor, proving convexity/stability conditions and deriving decay estimates verified by structure-preserving finite-element simulations.
motivation: Classical availability/entropy-based control of reactors is hard to reconcile with the Hamiltonian description of irreversible thermodynamics, so the authors seek a unified relative-energy framework that separates irreversible dissipation from profile-dependent terms while preserving the nonlinear PDE structure.
method: Starting from a thermodynamic duality between entropy-based availability and the relative Hamiltonian, the authors show strict convexity of the Hamiltonian density under positivity of heat capacity, compressibility and compositional susceptibility, decompose the relative Hamiltonian into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing parts, and design a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback; a coercivity condition yields a priori decay and a composite functional gives exponential stability for the linearized closed loop, checked with PFEM simulations.
result: An exact relative-energy balance is obtained with dissipation isolated, the closed loop is shown to be locally decaying for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions and exponentially stable in the linearized setting, and simulations confirm the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.
conclusion: Relative-energy port-Hamiltonian control provides a structure-preserving, thermodynamically consistent route to stabilizing spatially nonuniform reactor profiles without cancelling nonlinear dynamics, though the guarantees remain local/linearized.

title: Fundamental Limits Of Honest Inference With Heterogeneous Transfer Sources
authors: Yi Li Xuran Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transfer learning can improve precision by borrowing information from external sources, but how much improvement is possible while maintaining valid inference? We address this by studying honest confidence intervals for a target parameter using multiple sources with heterogeneous prespecified discrepancy bounds. Under local information and admissibility conditions, we establish a universal lower bound on interval length for procedures maintaining uniform coverage. A scalar information equation characterizes the bound, revealing how precision depends jointly on source sample sizes and discrepancies. Large source samples need not yield greater precision gains when their discrepancies are large. When discrepancies are unrestricted, honest intervals cannot improve upon the target-only rate, even when all sources are unbiased. For the Gaussian location model, we calculate optimal source weights and construct honest intervals attaining the lower bound order, establishing sharpness. We extend the lower bound theory to semiparametric models through parametric submodels. For the Cox proportional hazards model, we verify the information conditions under which the lower bound applies, including under right censoring.
tldr: This paper derives universal lower bounds on the length of honest confidence intervals when borrowing information from multiple heterogeneous transfer sources with prespecified discrepancy bounds.
motivation: Transfer learning promises precision gains from external data, but it is unclear how much improvement is achievable while preserving valid (uniformly covering) inference, especially when sources differ from the target in unknown or bounded ways.
method: Under local information and admissibility conditions, the authors establish a scalar information equation characterizing a lower bound on interval length for procedures with uniform coverage, and extend the analysis to semiparametric models via parametric submodels, including the Cox proportional hazards model with right censoring.
result: The bound shows precision depends jointly on source sample sizes and discrepancies; large source samples with large discrepancies need not help, and with unrestricted discrepancies honest intervals cannot beat the target-only rate even for unbiased sources. For the Gaussian location model, optimal source weights and order-sharp honest intervals are constructed.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental limits and matching constructions for information-borrowing inference, clarifying when heterogeneous transfer sources can and cannot yield genuine precision gains under honesty constraints.

title: Beyond Weak Convergence Of Signed Spectral Measures: Eigenvector Overlaps And High-dimensional Prediction Risk
authors: Thomas Stark, Georg K\"ostenberger, Nina D\"ornemann
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.
tldr: The paper replaces weak convergence of signed spectral measures with a bilinear-form convergence result to establish asymptotic prediction risk for spectral-filter estimators in high-dimensional regression.
motivation: Weak convergence of spectral measures, standardly proven via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms, breaks down for signed eigenvector-overlap measures in high-dimensional regression, so risk analyses built on it can be invalid.
method: The authors develop a novel risk-analysis approach based on convergence of bilinear forms rather than weak convergence, and characterize weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures via pointwise Stieltjes-transform convergence.
result: They prove convergence of prediction risk for estimators from arbitrary continuous spectral filters (including gradient descent and ridge regression) even without weak convergence, and give an explicit signed-measure integral representation yielding necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality of minimum-norm interpolation and tuned ridge regression.
conclusion: Bilinear-form convergence suffices where weak convergence fails, providing a rigorous and general framework for asymptotic risk of spectral-filter estimators in high-dimensional statistics.

title: Random Feature Policy Iteration For Inverse Mean Field Games With Complex Geometry And High Dimensions
authors: Xiangjian Zhang, Shanyin Tong, Xiaofeng Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a random feature policy iteration method for reconstructing the obstacle function in a mean-field game (MFG) from observations of its value function, leveraging the method's mesh-free nature and flexibility to handle complex geometries and high-dimensional problems. The method builds on a policy iteration framework for inverse MFGs, which decouples the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves. The fixed random feature representations preserve this linear structure, allowing the resulting subproblems to be solved by minimizing residuals at sampled collocation points through linear least-squares problems. The mesh-free nature of the method further extends the applicability of the policy iteration framework to inverse MFGs with complex geometry and in high dimensions. Another key advantage is its flexibility in using different spatial approximations for different variables: the obstacle function, value function, and population density can be represented in separate feature spaces, accommodating obstacles that are substantially less regular than the corresponding PDE solutions. Moreover, boundary conditions can be enforced through collocation on irregular domains without constructing boundary-fitted meshes. Numerical experiments involving smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.
tldr: The authors propose a random-feature policy iteration method for reconstructing obstacle functions in inverse mean-field games from value-function observations, designed to handle complex geometries and high dimensions.
motivation: Inverse mean-field games involve coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE systems that are hard to solve, and existing mesh-based approaches struggle with irregular domains and high-dimensional settings.
method: The policy iteration framework decouples the coupled PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse subproblems, which are solved via fixed random feature representations and linear least-squares residual minimization at collocation points, with separate feature spaces for obstacle, value function, and density.
result: Numerical experiments on smooth and discontinuous obstacles, domains with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate accuracy and flexibility of the mesh-free approach.
conclusion: Random feature policy iteration extends the applicability of inverse MFG solvers to complex geometries and high dimensions while accommodating irregular obstacle functions.

title: Sharpness Of The Acceleration-dependent H\"older Exponent For The Integrated Density Of States
authors: Jiangong You Jiabo Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent [MATH] for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer [MATH] and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree [MATH] such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is [MATH], and the exact local H\"older exponent is [MATH]. In particular, the [MATH]-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.
tldr: The paper proves sharpness of an acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent for the integrated density of states in the supercritical regime of quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators.
motivation: It addresses whether the known Hölder regularity of the integrated density of states in the subcritical regime extends to the supercritical regime for Diophantine frequencies.
method: The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix, together with comparison to an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization.
