result: For every positive integer and Diophantine frequency, the authors construct an even trigonometric polynomial potential with positive Lyapunov exponent at a spectral edge and exact local Hölder exponent matching the acceleration-dependent bound.
conclusion: The acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent is sharp in the supercritical regime, and the subcritical Hölder regularity does not hold generally in the supercritical setting.

title: Canard Explosions In Mass-action Networks With One Slow Direction
authors: Andrei-Dan Halanay Miruna-Mihaela Beldiman
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterised by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with [MATH] unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.
tldr: The paper analyzes canard explosions in mass-action chemical reaction networks with one slow direction using Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and algebraic criteria.
motivation: The authors aim to extend flux-based criteria for canard explosions from planar systems to mass-action networks with arbitrary species number and fast-subnetwork rank.
method: They express Krupa-Szmolyan derivatives and coefficients as rational functions of fluxes and reciprocal concentrations, derive planar and elementary-mode criteria, and use Farkas certificates, yield diagrams, and center-manifold reductions.
result: For rank-one fast subnetworks the criteria become linear in fluxes with an explicit cubic criticality; higher-rank cases require center-manifold corrections, illustrated in the Oregonator.
conclusion: The work provides proved algebraic and geometric conditions for canard explosions in mass-action networks, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multicontinuum Poroelasticity Model. Analysis And Computation
authors: Jing Zhang, Mohammed Al Kobaisi, Dmitry Ammosov, Jian Huang, Yunqing Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a macroscopic multicontinuum model for Biot poroelasticity. The full macroscopic multicontinuum system is derived by projecting the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces enriched with first-order multiscale corrections. This construction retains generalized pressure storage and coupling terms, with effective coefficients inherited from the microscopic bilinear forms. Under suitable coefficient assumptions, we establish well-posedness and energy stability of the macroscopic multicontinuum model. A fully discrete scheme combining the Galerkin finite element method in space with the backward Euler method in time is then developed. Its well-posedness and stability are proved, and a priori error estimates are derived using appropriate projection operators and energy arguments. Finally, numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate the accuracy of the multicontinuum model with respect to the averaged fine-scale solution.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes a macroscopic multicontinuum poroelasticity model with finite element discretization and error estimates.
motivation: It aims to capture multiscale behavior in Biot poroelasticity for high-contrast media using a multicontinuum projection approach.
method: The authors project the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces with first-order multiscale corrections, prove well-posedness and stability, and devise a fully discrete Galerkin finite element/backward Euler scheme with a priori error estimates.
result: Well-posedness, energy stability, and error estimates are established, and numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate accuracy against averaged fine-scale solutions.
conclusion: The multicontinuum poroelasticity model provides a rigorous macroscopic framework for multiscale Biot systems, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Weak Unit Reducibility Of The Eleventh Cyclotomic Field
authors: Yiyang Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the cyclotomic field [MATH] is unit reducible but not strongly unit reducible. So every nonzero principal fractional ideal of [MATH] has a generator that is a shortest nonzero vector. For [MATH], every shortest nonzero vector [MATH] satisfies [MATH]. The proof uses Sigrist's Hermite bound for cyclic forms and an averaging identity for cyclotomic units. For principal ideals in [MATH], ideal-SVP and the shortest-generator problem are polynomial-time equivalent.
tldr: The paper proves weak unit reducibility for the eleventh cyclotomic field and relates ideal-SVP to the shortest-generator problem in that setting.
motivation: Unit reducibility and shortest generators in cyclotomic fields are number-theoretic questions with connections to lattice problems such as ideal-SVP.
method: The proof uses Sigrist's Hermite bound for cyclic forms and an averaging identity for cyclotomic units.
result: The eleventh cyclotomic field is shown to be unit reducible but not strongly unit reducible, and for principal ideals ideal-SVP and the shortest-generator problem are polynomial-time equivalent.
conclusion: This is a pure number theory/lattice cryptography result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimization Of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding On Fully Node-Parallel Architectures For 5g Ldpc Codes
authors: Alexander von Bank, Oliver Griebel, Eike-Manuel Edelmann, Norbert Wehn, Laurent Schmalen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.
tldr: The paper proposes a Bayesian-optimization-based design method for iteration-agnostic lookup tables in min-RCQ LDPC decoding, improving energy efficiency on fully node-parallel architectures for 5G LDPC codes.
motivation: Finite-alphabet message passing decoders such as min-RCQ require well-designed lookup tables, and existing designs may not generalize across channels, modulation formats, or fully node-parallel architectures.
method: The authors use Bayesian optimization over a subspace of the LUT design space, with frame error rate as the loss function, requiring no channel or modulation knowledge, and apply it to irregular LDPC codes with puncturing and shortening.
result: The proposed iteration-agnostic LUTs achieve 38.6% better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum decoder without loss in error-correction performance.
conclusion: The design method is suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures and improves energy efficiency for 5G LDPC decoding, but it is a classical coding and hardware implementation contribution outside the specified quantum research directions.

title: Low Probability Of Target Detection In Wireless Sensing By Harnessing Reconfigurable-antenna Based Reflectors
authors: Yifan Zhang, Zhentian Zhang, Jantti Riku, Yichuan Wang, Xingwang Li, Tuo Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce low probability of target detection (LPTD) as a new security objective for wireless sensing systems, where the existence of a target is concealed from passive wardens. Unlike conventional communication security and covert communication, LPTD aims to protect the sensed target itself from malicious detection, rather than concealing transmitted signals or communication activities. Specifically, we propose a reconfigurable-antenna-based reflector-assisted target covertness scheme, where passive reflectors deployed around the target are harnessed as artificial scattering sources to confuse the warden. By adjusting their reflection coefficients, these reflectors reshape the local scattering environment and mask the target-induced echo. We then analyze the warden's optimal detection strategy and derive the false-alarm and missed-detection probabilities, followed by a closed-form expression for its minimum total detection error probability. Numerical results validate the analysis and show that sufficient cooperation among reflectors can increase the warden's minimum total detection error probability to approximately 0.94--0.96, making target detection close to random guessing.
tldr: The paper introduces low probability of target detection (LPTD) as a security metric for wireless sensing and shows that reconfigurable-antenna-based passive reflectors can mask a target's echo so that a warden's detection approaches random guessing.
motivation: Conventional communication security and covert communication hide transmitted signals or the act of communication, but not the sensed object itself; the authors aim to protect the sensed target from adversarial detection in wireless sensing systems.
method: Passive reflectors deployed around the target act as artificial scattering sources whose reflection coefficients are tuned to reshape the local scattering environment and obscure the target-induced echo; the warden's optimal detection strategy is analyzed, yielding false-alarm and missed-detection probabilities and a closed-form minimum total detection error probability.
result: Numerical results confirm the analysis and show that sufficient cooperation among reflectors raises the warden's minimum total detection error probability to roughly 0.94–0.96, making detection nearly equivalent to random guessing.
conclusion: Reflector-assisted scattering engineering provides an effective means of achieving target covertness in wireless sensing, establishing LPTD as a distinct security objective beyond classical covert communications.

title: CoordX Types: A Trustless, Swappable Type System For Shared Records
authors: Rob Ewin David Hyland-Wood
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The CoordX Protocol carries signed and encrypted entries between parties. It proves who wrote each entry and who had permission to write it. It does not say what an entry means. That task belongs above the protocol layer. This paper describes the CoordX type system, the layer that gives entries a meaning. A type is a short document that says how to read one part of a shared record: which entries count, what each position means, what a party may do there, and what a party must do next. The type system has two key properties. It is trustless: a type is an ordinary signed object fixed by its digest, and every party evaluates it for itself over entries that the CoordX Protocol has already verified. No party has to trust a server, a registry or another party's software. It is swappable: a type names the interpreter it is written for, so many interpreters, of different capabilities and designs, can be used side by side in one record. We describe how to write type schemas, and we define the expressive power of the schema language. Payloads form a regular language. Entry structure forms a regular tree language. Every rule and every computed value is a total function in the primitive recursive class, so evaluation always halts. We compare this with KQML, FIPA-ACL and CBCL, and we relate it to language-theoretic security.
tldr: The paper presents CoordX Types, a trustless and swappable type system layered above the CoordX protocol to assign meaning to signed and encrypted shared-record entries.
motivation: The CoordX Protocol verifies authorship and permissions for entries but does not define their semantics; a separate type layer is needed to specify how entries should be interpreted.
method: The authors define type schemas as signed, digest-fixed documents evaluated locally by each party, with swappable interpreters, and analyze the expressive power of the schema language using regular languages and primitive recursive functions.
result: Type payloads form a regular language, entry structures form a regular tree language, and all rules and computed values are total primitive recursive functions, guaranteeing halting evaluation.
conclusion: CoordX Types provides a decentralized semantic layer for shared records and is compared with KQML, FIPA-ACL, and CBCL, with connections to language-theoretic security.

title: AI-assisted Search For Self-compressing Gigawatt Subcycle Field Waveforms
authors: Aleksei M. Zheltikov, Youchan Park, Petr Zhokhov, Julia M. Mikhailova
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the physics behind pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and search for the optimal regimes of such compression over the parameter space as laid out by multimode nonlinear dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in gas-filled hollow fibers. With the pertinent physical criteria for pulse contrast and no pulse breakup formalized as operational stopping rules, a radical speedup of such search is achieved by delegating its tedious preliminary stages to generative pretrained transformer models. The precise adjustment of self-compression dynamics vis-a-vis the desired compressed pulse output is, however, not yet delegable to AI agents, as the criteria for such search are still largely subjective, operating with fine aspects of subcycle field structure, not yet formalizable as clear search-stopping instructions. An ultimate precision in such subcycle field engineering is attainable via a management of field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes, enabling pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and opening paths toward fiber-optic attosecond lightwave engineering.
tldr: This paper explores AI-assisted optimization of pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms in gas-filled hollow fibers.
motivation: The authors aim to speed up the search for optimal self-compression regimes by using transformer models for preliminary parameter exploration while retaining expert judgment for fine subcycle field structure.
method: They analyze multimode nonlinear dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in gas-filled hollow fibers, formalize contrast and no-breakup criteria as stopping rules, and delegate preliminary search stages to generative pretrained transformer models.
result: AI assistance enables radical speedup of the preliminary search, but precise tuning of self-compression dynamics remains not fully delegable due to subjective criteria involving fine subcycle field structure.
conclusion: Ultimate precision in subcycle field engineering is attainable through field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes, opening paths toward fiber-optic attosecond lightwave engineering.

title: Force-Dependent Change Of Structural Behavior Upon Pulling A Grafted Flexible Polymer
authors: Michael Bachmann J. Matthew Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulating polymer chains by means of experimental instruments such as optical tweezers has helped understand better the effects of molecular forces in macromolecular structures. In this study, we simulate the influence of a pulling force on structural phases of a coarse-grained model for flexible polymers using generalized-ensemble Monte Carlo methodologies. The recently introduced microcanonical inflection-point analysis method is employed to identify and classify structural phases of the system. Specific order parameters help characterize the transition behavior in response to the present pulling force. We show that, upon increasing the pulling strength, the coil-globule transition turns from second to first order, then merges with the liquid-solid transition. An intermediate phase, separating the coil and globule phases, is identified for certain force strengths. Clear evidence of the Gough-Joule effect is found as well. Transitions do not occur at all if the pulling force exceeds a certain threshold value.
tldr: Generalized-ensemble Monte Carlo simulations reveal how pulling forces reshape the structural phase diagram of a coarse-grained flexible polymer, including a force-induced change in the order of the coil-globule transition.
motivation: Optical tweezer experiments on single macromolecules motivate a systematic theoretical understanding of how mechanical force alters the structural phases and transitions of flexible polymers.
method: The authors simulate a coarse-grained flexible polymer under applied pulling force using generalized-ensemble Monte Carlo, and classify structural phases via microcanonical inflection-point analysis with suitable order parameters.
result: Increasing the pulling strength converts the coil-globule transition from second to first order and eventually merges it with the liquid-solid transition; an intermediate phase appears at certain forces, the Gough-Joule effect is observed, and no transitions occur above a threshold force.
conclusion: Mechanical tension qualitatively reorganizes the polymer phase behavior, providing a statistical-physics framework for interpreting force spectroscopy experiments on macromolecules.

title: Locating Debunkers For Rumor Mitigation In Directed Networks
authors: Kasra Ghorbani, Xinshan Jiao, Tao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rumors can spread widely through social networks, making the selection of a limited number of debunkers to disseminate corrective information important. Existing centrality-based methods only consider the individual influence of a node on spreading processes. Those individually influential nodes often have heavily overlapping influence ranges, resulting in a limited number of users they can cover. To address this problem, we propose the so-called Hybrid Marginal Influence (HMI) framework, which combines node centrality with additional audience coverage provided by each candidate and adaptively balances these two factors through a greedy selection procedure. We further develop the Debunker-Augmented SIR (DA-SIR) model for the propagation of rumors and corrective information. Experiments on ten real-world directed networks show that HMI generally selects debunkers with broader audience coverage than conventional centrality-based methods, accompanied by a lower final cumulative fraction of users who repost the rumor.
tldr: The paper proposes a Hybrid Marginal Influence (HMI) greedy framework for selecting debunkers in directed social networks to mitigate rumor spreading.
motivation: Existing centrality-based debunker selection ignores the heavy overlap in influence ranges among individually central nodes, limiting the total audience actually reached by corrective information.
method: HMI combines node centrality with the marginal audience coverage each candidate adds, adaptively balancing the two via a greedy selection procedure, and a Debunker-Augmented SIR (DA-SIR) model is developed to simulate rumor and correction co-propagation.
result: Across ten real-world directed networks, HMI selects debunkers with broader audience coverage than conventional centrality baselines and yields a lower final cumulative fraction of users reposting the rumor.
conclusion: Accounting for marginal coverage rather than raw centrality alone gives more effective debunker placement for rumor mitigation in directed networks.

title: Discrete Total Variation Under The Multinomial, Part 5: Cyclic Total Variation
authors: Neven Elezovi\'c Nikola Bani\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses to \(\beta_c(n)=\beta_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(\gamma_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/\beta_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.
tldr: This paper analyzes the variance and asymptotic behavior of cyclic discrete total variation under a uniform multinomial law, proving a ridge-localization result for the linear-variance optimizer.
motivation: The authors aim to extend previous results on discrete total variation by adding a wrap-around edge and deriving exact asymptotic coefficients for the cyclic statistic.
method: The analysis uses covariance-block multiplicities, a cyclic-linear transfer identity, and uniform control of three ridge blocks to study the variance profile and optimizer.
result: The cyclic variance simplifies to a bin-independent leading coefficient with a linear constant-order correction, and the heuristic sqrt(N) mode law is upgraded to a theorem on compact ridge windows.
conclusion: The paper provides rigorous asymptotic results for cyclic discrete total variation, though the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open.

title: Orthogonal Splines Associated To Root Systems And Applications To Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
authors: Dionel Jaime
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline [MATH] with [MATH]-dimensional direction set [MATH] and associated differential operator [MATH]. Assuming that each direction in [MATH] appears with even multiplicity i.e [MATH], we may endow [MATH] with a special inner product [MATH] which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order [MATH]. Then, for the special case when the directions in [MATH] are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for [MATH]. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under [MATH] (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation. Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for [MATH], the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into [MATH] is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under [MATH], this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When [MATH] comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if [MATH] is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate [MATH] from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.
tldr: The paper constructs bi-orthogonal spline systems tied to root systems and uses them to build local quasi-interpolation operators with optimal approximation order from generalized derivative samples.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize box-spline approximation theory by exploiting root-system structure and a Sobolev-like inner product to obtain well-behaved dual bases and quasi-interpolants.
method: Assuming even multiplicities of directions, they endow the principal shift-invariant spline space with a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product and construct compactly supported bi-orthogonal bases, then define analysis-synthesis operators via integration by parts.
result: The resulting operators are local discrete quasi-interpolants, and for irreducible root systems they can be modified to achieve optimal approximation order from generalized derivative samples.
conclusion: Root-system-based orthogonal splines provide a flexible framework for derivative-based function approximation with uniformly sparse truncated-power representations.

title: A Family Of Alternating Projection Examples Whose Ces\`aro Means Fail To Converge Strongly
authors: Tran Thanh Tung Heinz H. Bauschke
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1965, Bregman proved that the sequence of iterates of the method of alternating projections applied to two closed convex sets with nonempty intersection in a Hilbert space converges weakly to a point in the intersection. The question whether this convergence may actually fail to be strong was settled in a seminal paper by Hundal in 2004. He provided a counterexample featuring a halfspace and a closed convex cone generated by a certain curve. While largely elementary, the details of Hundal's construction and analysis are quite involved. We revisit this seminal example and present a family of such examples that allows for simpler proofs. Our generating curve combines unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a height determined by a scalar function. The orbits converge weakly --- but not strongly --- to the origin, while their norms have a positive limit for which we give explicit lower bounds. We also prove that the associated Ces\`aro means behave likewise; in fact, this is generalized to alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point. Finally, these orbits allow interpretations in the context of projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.
tldr: The paper constructs a family of examples showing that the method of alternating projections and its Cesàro means can converge weakly but not strongly, generalizing Hundal's 2004 counterexample with simpler proofs.
motivation: Bregman's 1965 weak convergence theorem left open whether strong convergence can fail; Hundal settled this in 2004 with a technically involved construction, which the authors aim to simplify and generalize.
method: The authors build generating curves from unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a scalar height function, then analyze orbits of alternating projections and alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point.
result: The orbits converge weakly to the origin but not strongly, with norms having a positive limit for which explicit lower bounds are given; the same behavior holds for Cesàro means.
conclusion: The construction yields a broad family of counterexamples with elementary proofs, with interpretations in projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.

title: Automating The Derivation Of Advanced Algorithms In Numerical Linear Algebra Using Associative Algebras With Involution
authors: Ran Gutin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the [MATH]-square root and [MATH] indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these [MATH]-algebras. The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real [MATH]-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path [MATH]-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices. Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable [MATH]-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined. Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on [MATH] real matrices.
tldr: This thesis generalizes standard numerical linear algebra algorithms to scalars in associative algebras with involution, organizing decompositions via doubly-signed quivers and implementing the framework in Python.
motivation: The work aims to automate the derivation of advanced numerical linear algebra algorithms by overloading seven scalar operations, analogous to automatic differentiation, so that many decompositions reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over generalized algebras.
method: It develops a quiver-based algebraic framework for real *-algebras, proves a Gabriel-type theorem, and reinterprets spectral decompositions, SVD, Takagi factorization, Jordan forms, and algorithms such as QR/LR and Cholesky/LU through generalized unitary similarity problems.
result: The thesis shows that over split-complex numbers the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm two steps at a time, Cholesky becomes Doolittle LU, and infinitesimal computations connect Gram-Schmidt to Bruhat decomposition and Gaussian elimination to Dijkstra's algorithm.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified algebraic automation of numerical linear algebra algorithms, with a Python library implementing the operations and visualizations, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Message-Passing-Based Bayesian Joint Channel Estimation And Data Detection For Pilot-Guard-Free Afdm
authors: Yuan Zhengdao, Guo Qinghua, Jin Ming, Liu Zilong, Xiao Pei
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing channel estimation methods for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) over doubly dispersive channels commonly isolate pilots and data with pilot guard symbols, resulting in substantial transmission overhead, while fractional Doppler introduces off-grid mismatch and complicates accurate channel estimation. This paper develops a pilot-guard-free AFDM transmission and reception scheme with a Bayesian receiver for joint channel estimation and data symbol detection. Uniformly interleaved pilots are embedded among data symbols without dedicated guard symbols, and the resulting pilot-data coupling is explicitly incorporated into the joint inference problem rather than suppressed through guard-based isolation.
tags: joint channel estimation and data detection
tldr: The paper proposes a pilot-guard-free AFDM transmission scheme with a Bayesian message-passing receiver for joint channel estimation and data detection over doubly dispersive channels.
motivation: Existing AFDM channel estimation methods use pilot guard symbols, causing high overhead, and fractional Doppler causes off-grid mismatch that complicates accurate estimation.
method: Uniformly interleaved pilots are embedded among data symbols without guard symbols, and the induced pilot-data coupling is incorporated into a joint Bayesian inference problem solved via message passing.
result: The scheme aims to reduce transmission overhead while handling fractional Doppler and pilot-data coupling for improved joint channel estimation and symbol detection.
conclusion: The work is a classical wireless communications signal-processing contribution and has no apparent connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
keywords: joint channel estimation and data detection

title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method For Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization
authors: Wanqi Hou, Yanzhen Peng, Chao Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an [MATH] best-residual bound holds over [MATH] accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.
tldr: The paper develops a structure-preserving inexact augmented Lagrangian method for semidefinite complementarity-constrained optimization and establishes stationarity and convergence guarantees.
motivation: Semidefinite complementarity constraints appear in inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization, but existing methods may not preserve matrix structure or provide strong stationarity guarantees.
method: The authors propose SPALM, which augments smooth constraints while retaining matrix complementarity in subproblems, solved via an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions.
result: They prove asymptotic M-stationarity, M-stationarity under AM-regularity, sufficient conditions via active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ, residual convergence, and a best-residual bound; numerical experiments pass feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.
conclusion: The method provides a theoretically grounded approach for semidefinite complementarity optimization, including a lifted model for rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation.

title: Understanding The Asymptotic Transience Of Q-Learning Via Distributional Expansion
authors: Shengbo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale [MATH], whereas the maximization transient is of order [MATH] and converges almost surely, after rescaling by [MATH], to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.
tldr: A refined asymptotic analysis of synchronous Q-learning that separates the transient error into a Gaussian TD component and a nonnegative maximization-induced displacement converging to a random limit.
motivation: Standard central-limit Gaussian approximations erase the transient error that is empirically prominent in Q-learning, while worst-case finite-sample bounds obscure instance-specific mechanisms.
method: Decomposes the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference component and a maximization-induced displacement, then analyzes the rescaled transient limit and applies an Edgeworth expansion to the TD component.
result: The maximization transient scales as a lower order than the Gaussian TD fluctuations and, after rescaling, converges almost surely to a random limit; Edgeworth corrections separate initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuation, and maximization effects.
conclusion: The analysis yields an asymptotically exact instance-level characterization of Q-learning transient error and explains how sub-central-limit effects persist.

title: A Monotone Meshfree-Particle Method For Mean Field Games On Scattered Point Clouds
authors: Linyu Peng Jiongyi Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a monotone meshfree--particle method for mean field games (MFGs). We discretize the backward Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation on a fixed scattered cloud, transport the forward Fokker--Planck law with reflected and killed particles, and close the fictitious-play loop by interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation. Monotonicity is imposed row by row on two-dimensional clouds. Each row combines a positive generalized finite difference Laplacian with a nonnegative decomposition of the drift along rays to surrounding visible neighbors, with mirror images at reflecting walls, and every fixed-policy matrix is an M-matrix for arbitrary cell-P\'eclet number. We prove a discrete comparison principle and, on polygons with re-entrant corners included, that one HJB solve at a prescribed density converges to the viscosity solution off the boundary vertices, for convex Hamiltonians of at most quadratic growth under a structure condition. On a two-room floor plan with re-entrant door jambs, the computed HJB solutions converge to exact ones. A source-free exact MFG tests the fully coupled computation. At matched degrees of freedom on a grid domain, the meshfree HJB solve has a larger [MATH] error and a smaller [MATH] error than a five-point finite-difference solve, and is about twice as expensive including the stencil construction. On a non-convex evacuation game, the interior nodes of nine clouds receive monotone rows, apart from a few next to the boundary vertices that copy a neighbor.
tldr: The paper introduces a monotone meshfree-particle numerical method for mean field games on scattered point clouds.
motivation: Mean field games require robust numerical schemes for coupled HJB and Fokker-Planck equations, especially on complex or non-grid geometries.
method: The authors discretize the HJB equation on a fixed scattered cloud with row-wise monotone stencils and transport the Fokker-Planck law using reflected and killed particles, closing the fictitious-play loop via interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation.
result: They prove a discrete comparison principle and convergence to the viscosity solution for convex Hamiltonians under a structure condition, and demonstrate convergence on a two-room floor plan and an evacuation game.
conclusion: The method provides a monotone meshfree approach for MFGs on scattered clouds, though it is more expensive than finite differences and is not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Star Monotone Operators: Theory And Applications
authors: Felipe Lara Phan Quoc Khanh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Introduced by Solodov and Svaiter , star monotone operators have repeatedly appeared as a sufficient condition ensuring global convergence of first-order algorithms, without requiring full monotonicity. Yet, despite this recurring role, a systematic study of the class itself has been missing from the literature. This paper fills that gap with the first comprehensive treatment of star monotone operators, a class that strictly encompasses monotone and pseudomonotone operators with nonempty zero sets, together with operators that are strongly quasimonotone along rays and satisfy a radial nondegeneracy condition. We develop basic calculus rules, existence and uniqueness results for zeros, global metric subregularity, and precise structural relationships with classical monotonicity notions. We further demonstrate the versatility of star monotonicity through a Clarke subdifferential characterization of nonsmooth star quasiconvexity, applications to Minty and Stampacchia variational inequalities, linear convergence guarantees for subgradient-type methods, and separable operators related to the Debreu--Koopmans problem.
tldr: The paper provides the first systematic treatment of star monotone operators, a class generalizing monotone and pseudomonotone operators that guarantees convergence of first-order algorithms.
motivation: Star monotonicity has repeatedly appeared as a sufficient condition for global convergence of first-order methods without full monotonicity, yet no systematic study of the operator class itself existed.
method: The authors develop calculus rules, existence and uniqueness results for zeros, global metric subregularity, and structural relationships with classical monotonicity notions, plus applications to variational inequalities and subgradient methods.
result: They establish a Clarke subdifferential characterization of nonsmooth star quasiconvexity, Minty/Stampacchia variational inequality applications, linear convergence guarantees for subgradient-type methods, and separable operator results tied to the Debreu–Koopmans problem.
conclusion: Star monotone operators form a rich, strictly broader class than monotone and pseudomonotone operators, offering a unified framework for convergence analysis in nonsmooth optimization.

title: Zero-Hopf Networks
authors: Manuela Aguiar, Ana Dias, Fahimeh Mokhtari
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.
tldr: The paper introduces and classifies zero-Hopf networks, regular coupled-cell networks whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a purely imaginary eigenvalue pair, and analyzes their generic codimension-one bifurcations and synchrony spaces.
motivation: Zero-Hopf bifurcations are important in dynamical systems with a zero eigenvalue and a purely imaginary pair, and the authors aim to understand when such bifurcations occur generically in network-admissible vector fields.
method: The authors use adjacency matrices and associated eigenvector structures of regular networks, prove existence of infinitely many zero-Hopf networks, and classify connected 4-cell valency-two regular networks up to permutation while computing normal forms via the Rink-Sanders method.
result: They show an infinite family of zero-Hopf networks supporting generic codimension-one zero-Hopf bifurcation, present general results on synchrony spaces for four-cell networks, and classify nine distinct connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two.
conclusion: The work provides a network-based characterization of zero-Hopf bifurcations, showing that input symmetry restricts normal-form simplifications although the classified networks share a common coupling function normal form.

title: Who Moved The Frontier? Paying Open Frontier Challenges With Free Identities
authors: Duc V. Le Luca Zanolini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an open frontier challenge, anyone, person or AI agent, submits changes to a shared problem, and a change that beats the best measured score becomes the public baseline. How should it pay when identities are free? Rank prizes can be gamed: on a replay of one track of a recent challenge, one solver's steps under two identities would have taken first and second prize. We consider a prediction-market rule, proposed for machine-learning contests, that pays each accepted step for the progress it adds; with exact scores, among rules that see only a step's start and end, only these resist splitting and merging, and extra identities gain nothing. With noisy scores and independent normal runs, we prove that any payment that never takes money back and pays real improvements also pays something, on average, to a change that does nothing. We propose a fee per submission, at least what luck pays per attempt, that removes each attempt's expected profit if verifiers are honest and no submission is noisier than planned; nothing enforces that bound, and under noise the rule does not cap the total paid. If crediting another and faking credit to one's second account look the same, a rule that neither rewards fakes nor punishes honesty pays for credit at most what lying costs. We introduce a royalty on how much a later gain falls without the earlier change, which needs no claims but needs removable changes. For five public challenges, we name the rule our results would support.
tldr: The paper designs and analyzes payment rules for open 'frontier' challenges (e.g., ML leaderboards) that remain fair when participants can create unlimited free identities.
motivation: Rank-based prizes in open challenges can be gamed by submitting under multiple identities, so a payment scheme is needed that rewards genuine progress rather than rank position.
method: It formalizes properties such as resistance to splitting and merging of submissions, proves impossibility results for noisy scores with independent normal runs, and proposes a per-submission fee and a royalty mechanism based on counterfactual gain.
result: Only progress-based (prediction-market-style) rules that see a step's start and end resist splitting and merging with exact scores; under noise, any rule that never reclaims money and pays real improvements also pays, on average, for no-op changes, unless a submission fee is imposed.
conclusion: The authors identify which payment rules are incentive-compatible for identity-free open challenges, propose fees and royalties to curb noise-driven and fake-credit exploitation, and map their results onto five public challenges.

title: Hijacking A Trusted Llm In Real-World Quantized Deployments Only Requires A Disguised Adapter
authors: Jiayang Li, Tianqing Zhu, Huan Huo, Heng Xu, Shang Wang, Wanlei Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-party low-rank adaptation (LoRA) adapters are tailored to perform decision tasks such as content moderation and function selection. However, in the real world, quantized deployments carry a potential threat in that an adapter can pass an audit with the unquantized base, yet hijack decisions when the same base is quantized for deployment. Demonstrating this threat requires an adapter that preserves benign behavior before quantization, but hijacks decisions afterward. Further, this must hold without modifying the trusted base or knowing the victim's quantization configuration. We therefore present QHijack-LoRA, an adapter-only attack that uses the base model's natural quantization residual to activate decision hijacking. The attacker modifies neither the trusted base model nor the victim's quantization configuration. With QHijack-LoRA, a four-objective training procedure separates full-precision dormancy from quantized target activation, while preserving clean-input behavior. The adapter is trained across several different quantization methods, while adaptive reweighting and residual-direction augmentation extend the attack to unseen configurations. Our results show that auditing performed exclusively under full-precision conditions does not provide assurance of decision integrity in quantized deployment environments. Thus, we also propose a cross-precision paired audit that checks the candidate adapter in its intended deployment configuration. This work shows the critical need to audit third-party adapters in any potential quantized deployment.
tldr: The paper introduces QHijack-LoRA, an adapter-only attack that stays dormant under full-precision auditing of a trusted LLM base but hijacks decision behavior once the base is quantized for deployment.
motivation: Third-party LoRA adapters are widely used for tasks like content moderation and function selection, and quantization is standard in deployment; the authors argue that an adapter audited only in full precision can still compromise decisions after quantization, so a cross-precision paired audit is needed.
method: A four-objective training procedure separates full-precision dormancy from quantization-activated hijacking, exploiting the base model's natural quantization residual without altering the base or knowing the victim's quantization configuration, with adaptive reweighting and residual-direction augmentation for generalization across quantization methods.
result: The adapter preserves benign clean-input behavior in full precision yet reliably hijacks decisions across several quantization schemes, including unseen configurations, showing full-precision-only auditing gives no assurance of post-quantization integrity.
conclusion: Third-party adapters must be audited in their intended quantized deployment configuration, motivating the proposed cross-precision paired audit.

title: Protecting Sensitive Knowledge Under Llm Unlearning: The Proxy Threat And A Superposition-Aware Defense
authors: Jiayang Li, Tianqing Zhu, Longxiang Gao, Huajie Chen, Dayong Ye, Shang Wang, Huan Huo, Wanlei Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine unlearning lets the owner of large language models (LLMs) remove specific entities from a trained model without retraining from scratch. Existing machine unlearning methods focus on removing the requested entities while maintaining utility. However, we observe that the representations of distinct entities in an LLM may overlap in shared parameter subspaces, a phenomenon known as knowledge superposition. Removing one entity may then affect other entities. This exposes a new security threat: legitimate unlearning requests can be exploited to remove sensitive entities that were never requested. This threat is unlike data poisoning or backdoor attacks. We define the attack as the Proxy Unlearning Attack (PUA), which selects removable proxy entities superposed with a sensitive target. The attack can even occur unintentionally, when benign users accidentally remove entities superposed with a sensitive one. In response, we propose Superposition-Aware Unlearning Protection (SAUP), a general defense framework that can be applied to unlearning requests to ensure a correct removal. SAUP performs in two stages. Before unlearning, it uses superposition detection to estimate which sensitive entities the request puts at risk. After unlearning, it decouples the shared representations and restores the affected entities, while keeping the requested entities suppressed. Our findings reveal that legitimate unlearning requests can be maliciously exploited through knowledge superposition. When dealing with unlearning requests, LLM providers need representation-level detection and recovery mechanisms to mitigate this threat and protect sensitive knowledge.
tldr: The paper identifies a Proxy Unlearning Attack in LLM unlearning, where unlearning requests can inadvertently or maliciously remove sensitive knowledge due to superposed representations, and proposes a two-stage defense called SAUP.
motivation: Existing LLM unlearning methods aim to remove requested entities while preserving utility, but knowledge superposition can cause unlearning of one entity to affect others, creating a security risk for sensitive knowledge.
method: The authors define the Proxy Unlearning Attack, selecting proxy entities whose representations overlap with sensitive targets, and propose Superposition-Aware Unlearning Protection (SAUP), which detects risky superpositions before unlearning and decouples/restores affected representations afterward.
result: The findings show that legitimate unlearning requests can be exploited or accidentally remove sensitive entities through shared parameter subspaces, and SAUP mitigates this by protecting superposed sensitive knowledge while suppressing requested entities.
conclusion: LLM providers need representation-level detection and recovery mechanisms when handling unlearning requests to prevent proxy attacks and protect sensitive knowledge.

title: One Fabrication Is Enough: A Fake News Article Changes The Forecasts Of Llm Forecasting Systems
authors: Bradly C. Stadie Zeyu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used for forecasting, and the best forecasting systems retrieve news as evidence to strengthen their predictions. This also opens them to attack. We study the weakest attacker of this kind, who knows only the forecasting question and publishes fabricated news articles, with no access to the model, the retriever or its queries. We evaluate how far this attack reaches on stock questions and real prediction-market questions. Once the article is in the model's context, it reverses 74% to 82% of the forecasts that opposed it, on every frontier model we tested. The model cannot verify the fabrication and follows it anyway. Retrieval is the attack's entry point, and the systems built to retrieve well are the most exposed: the architectures of two leading deployed forecasting systems, whose agents search for every related article, retrieve the fabricated one in about 90% of runs. Accuracy cannot reveal this harm: the attacked forecaster is right when the attacker's direction turns out right and wrong otherwise, so its average accuracy barely changes while its forecasts follow the attacker's guess. We also propose a second attacker, who publishes two articles that argue opposite directions to make the forecaster unsure. The model does not hedge; it returns a confident forecast in a direction the attacker no longer controls. We then evaluate the two strongest published retrieval-time defenses, passage filtering and partitioned retrieval. Each stops the one-article attack but is bypassed by a one-prompt change to the attack. Together they stop both bypasses at four articles, but sixteen distorted copies beat them, and they change 29% of clean decisions and discard 39% of the genuine news. Partitioned retrieval also requires control of the retrieval index. Systems that search the open web have no such control and are left with the filter alone. For them, the attack still works.
tldr: A fake news article injected into a forecasting LLM's retrieved context can reverse 74-82% of opposing forecasts, and standard retrieval-time defenses are easily bypassed.
motivation: LLMs are increasingly used as forecasting systems that retrieve news as evidence, which creates an attack surface exploitable by an adversary who knows only the forecasting question.
method: The authors introduce a weak black-box attacker that publishes fabricated articles, test it on stock and prediction-market questions across frontier models, and then evaluate retrieval-time defenses (passage filtering, partitioned retrieval) against progressively stronger attacks.
result: The one-article attack flips 74-82% of opposing forecasts and is retrieved in ~90% of runs by two deployed systems; defenses stop the simple attack but fail against prompt-level bypasses and multi-copy distortions, while degrading clean accuracy by 29%.
conclusion: Accuracy metrics cannot detect this manipulation, and open-web retrieval systems lack index control, leaving them vulnerable to fabrication attacks.

title: Typed Knowledge Over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory For Verified Science
authors: Hans-Martin Will
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematical proof assistants such as Coq, Agda, and Lean 4 build proof irrelevance into definitional conversion ([MATH] for [MATH] with [MATH]), erasing which derivation established a theorem. While natural for mathematics over fixed axioms, judgmental proof irrelevance is incompatible with verified scientific stores, which must inspect and compare independent derivations of the same claim to assess consilience and compute counterfactual retractions when an assay, reagent, or model is invalidated. Moreover, combining definitional proof irrelevance with subsingleton elimination breaks strong normalization and renders algorithmic conversion non-transitive. We present the type-theoretic and institutional foundations of Eigenius, a verified knowledge substrate for science. First, we formulate a dependent kernel with cumulative universes ([MATH]), impredicative [MATH], inductive families with index-forced subsingleton elimination, and intensional identity types, where definitional equality [MATH] is untyped joinability under an orthogonal CRS and proof irrelevance is a witnessed propositional axiom ([MATH]). Second, we unify universe cumulativity, codomain-covariant [MATH]-subtyping, and ontology class inclusions in a coercion-free subsumption judgment whose bidirectional fragments ([MATH]) satisfy subject reduction and are sound and complete for declarative typing. Third, we organize external verifiers into a three-level institutional hierarchy with explicit axiom policies (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), internalize a justification logic with Why-provenance semiring support [MATH], and embed Cooper's Type Theory with Records (TTR) to type open-world knowledge graphs. Finally, we prove consistency in Grothendieck universes and mechanize the metatheory in Lean 4 with zero sorry axioms.
tldr: The paper introduces Eigenius, a proof-relevant dependent type theory with cumulative universes and an institutional hierarchy of external verifiers, aimed at building verified scientific knowledge stores that retain and compare distinct derivations rather than erasing them via proof irrelevance.
motivation: Proof assistants like Coq, Agda, and Lean 4 build judgmental proof irrelevance into conversion, which is natural for mathematics but unsuitable for scientific knowledge bases that must inspect independent derivations to assess consilience and support counterfactual retractions; moreover, combining definitional proof irrelevance with subsingleton elimination breaks strong normalization and transitivity of algorithmic conversion.
method: The authors formulate a dependent kernel with cumulative universes, impredicative Prop, inductive families with index-forced subsingleton elimination, and intensional identity types where definitional equality is untyped joinability under an orthogonal combinatory reduction system, with proof irrelevance as a witnessed propositional axiom; they also unify cumulativity, subtyping and ontology class inclusion in a coercion-free subsumption judgment, organize external verifiers into a three-level institutional hierarchy, internalize a justification logic with Why-provenance semirings, and embed Type Theory with Records.
result: Bidirectional fragments of the subsumption judgment satisfy subject reduction and are sound and complete for declarative typing; consistency is proved in Grothendieck universes and the metatheory is mechanized in Lean 4 without sorry axioms.
conclusion: Proof-relevant type theory with institutional verification provides a principled foundation for verified scientific knowledge substrates, though the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: MetaCom: Meta Codebook Learning For Robust V2x Semantic Communications
authors: Muge Yu, Danlan Huang, Xinyi Zhou, Shuqi Chai, Zhiyong Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collaborative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks faces dual challenges: strictly limited bandwidth and channel impairments. Existing static quantization schemes often suffer from feature manifold drift caused by highly non-stationary traffic environments. To address this, we propose MetaCom, a robust digital semantic communication framework featuring a Meta-Codebook Learning paradigm. First, we introduce a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications (DQSemCom) module trained with perturbations induced by the simulated digital modulation and channel via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. Building on this, we design a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism (Bi-MEM) that treats manifold drift as a sequence of rapid adaptation tasks, aligning the codebook via data-level smoothing and parameter-level meta-updates. Furthermore, we validate MetaCom under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Experimental results demonstrate that MetaCom achieves superior trade-offs between perception precision and communication overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin under low-SNR conditions.
tldr: MetaCom proposes a meta-codebook learning framework for robust digital semantic communication in V2X networks under channel impairments.
motivation: Collaborative V2X perception is constrained by limited bandwidth and non-stationary channel conditions, which cause feature manifold drift in static quantization schemes.
method: The paper introduces a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications module trained with simulated modulation/channel perturbations via Gumbel-Softmax, plus a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism for codebook adaptation.
result: Experiments under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading show improved perception-overhead trade-offs and significant gains over state-of-the-art methods at low SNR.
conclusion: Meta-codebook learning can improve robustness of digital semantic communication for V2X collaborative perception, but the work is outside quantum information science.

title: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination For Multi-Cell Xl-mimo Under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity
authors: Muhammad Shoaib Ayub, Rana Muhammad Subhan, Insoo Koo, Felipe Augusto Pereira de Figueiredo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial non-stationarity in multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) confines each user to a visibility region (VR) of each array. VR-Net exploits these regions for subarray-level coordinated beamforming. A base-station (BS)-indexed conflict graph identifies overlapping VRs; gain-based association and a masked multi-cell weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) iteration restrict beam design and channel state information (CSI) uploads to the relevant subarray blocks. We establish conditions for exact per-cell decoupling, derive the expected CSI loads, bound the loss of designing on the VR-gated channel and the loss of the support constraint, and characterize single-edge visibility contrast through a closed-form Fresnel transition width. Simulations use a 3GPP TR 38.901 Release-19-based near-field UMi channel with modular facade arrays and pre-registered criteria. At a 30 dB threshold, VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of the full-aperture WMMSE sum rate in every tested setting while uploading 10-39% fewer complex CSI entries. It gains up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz over an all-user adaptation of the multi-cell scheme of P\'erez-Ad\'an et al. at moderate power and dense load, and inter-cell coordination adds up to 33% over per-cell design.
tldr: VR-Net is a subarray-level coordinated beamforming scheme for multi-cell XL-MIMO that exploits near-field spatial non-stationarity and visibility regions to reduce CSI upload while preserving sum-rate performance.
motivation: Extremely large-scale MIMO arrays in multi-cell deployments exhibit near-field spatial non-stationarity, where each user sees only part of each array, creating opportunities and challenges for efficient coordinated beamforming and CSI acquisition.
method: The authors construct a BS-indexed conflict graph from overlapping visibility regions, use gain-based user association, and develop a masked multi-cell WMMSE iteration that restricts beam design and CSI uploads to relevant subarray blocks; they also derive decoupling conditions, CSI load estimates, and loss bounds.
result: Simulations with a 3GPP near-field UMi channel show that VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of full-aperture WMMSE sum rate at a 30 dB threshold while reducing complex CSI entries by 10-39%, and it outperforms an all-user multi-cell baseline by up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz.
conclusion: Subarray-level coordination based on visibility regions can significantly reduce CSI overhead in multi-cell XL-MIMO while maintaining near-optimal sum-rate performance, with inter-cell coordination providing substantial gains over per-cell design.

title: Chinese Whispers About Vulnerabilities
authors: Jukka Ruohonen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dissemination of information about known software vulnerabilities occurs online in various ways. Everything from email and development systems to social media are used. Given this variety and a dataset of about 382 thousand online references for about 55 thousand vulnerabilities, the paper demonstrates that the referenced online information sources tend to be mostly dissimilar statistically. The mean cosine similarity between them is only 0.22. Interestingly, the amounts of online references neither increase nor decrease similarity between the online information sources. In contrast, vulnerabilities primarily associated with GitHub and programming language ecosystems tend to have more dissimilar online references than other vulnerabilities. Also vulnerability reports, whether in bug tracking systems or bug bounty platforms, tend to increase dissimilarity. With these empirical results, the paper contributes to the efforts to narrow an enduring knowledge gap related to the online tracking and associated traceability of software vulnerabilities.
tldr: This paper empirically analyzes the statistical dissimilarity of online information sources about known software vulnerabilities.
motivation: The author aims to address a knowledge gap in the online tracking and traceability of software vulnerabilities across diverse platforms.
method: Using a dataset of roughly 382 thousand online references for about 55 thousand vulnerabilities, the paper computes cosine similarity between referenced sources and examines how similarity varies with reference counts and vulnerability ecosystems.
result: Online information sources are mostly dissimilar, with a mean cosine similarity of only 0.22; more references do not increase similarity, while GitHub, programming-language ecosystems, bug trackers, and bug bounty platforms tend to increase dissimilarity.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding vulnerability information dissemination and highlight the fragmented nature of online vulnerability tracking.

title: What You See Is (Not) What You Got: The Human Factor In Pdf Signature Verification
authors: Jakob Heher, Emanuel Pichler, Stefan More
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Signed PDF documents have legally binding value under frameworks such as the EU's eIDAS regulation. In this work, we present Genuine PDF Forgeries, a novel attack class that focuses on human factors in signature validation. Our attacks target the disconnect between cryptographically verifiable signer certificates and human-visible signature blocks embedded in documents. We analyze our attacks against 23 PDF viewers and validation tools across desktop platforms and the web. We find that nine of the 13 viewers that automatically report signature validity hide authenticated signer information behind additional user interaction. We then evaluate the attack in twin deception-based online studies with 584 EU-based participants. To further validate the impact, we perform a highly tailored real-world attack study with six trials within two privacy-sensitive organizations. Five of six organizational trials accepted requests authenticated using the forged visual identity. In the online studies (total n=584), the most effective attack variant deceives 71.9% of eligible participants on first impression, and 57.3% continue to be deceived even after we prompt for additional introspection. We derive viewer-side countermeasures and prototype a safeguard that overlays the untrusted signature block with signer information obtained from the validated certificate. Our results show that boolean validity indicators, not associated with the authenticated signer identity, are insufficient in practice.
tldr: The paper introduces 'Genuine PDF Forgeries,' a human-factors attack on PDF signature verification that exploits the gap between cryptographic signer identity and visually displayed signature blocks.
motivation: Signed PDFs have legal weight under frameworks like eIDAS, but users may trust misleading visual signature indicators even when cryptographic validation occurs.
method: The authors design and test forgery variants against 23 PDF viewers/tools, run two deception-based online studies with 584 EU participants, and conduct six real-world trials in privacy-sensitive organizations.
result: Nine of 13 viewers that report signature validity hide authenticated signer information behind extra interaction; the best attack deceives 71.9% of eligible participants initially and 57.3% after prompting, with 5 of 6 organizational trials accepting forged visual identities.
conclusion: Boolean validity indicators without authenticated signer identity are insufficient; viewer-side countermeasures such as overlaying validated certificate information on untrusted signature blocks are needed.

title: The Golden Ratio: Ef1 And Ordinal-MMS For Additive Goods
authors: Shraddha Pathak Hadi Hosseini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every complete allocation that is envy-free up to one good (EF1) guarantees each of the [MATH] agents her [MATH]-out-of-[MATH] maximin share. Can we construct allocations that satisfy EF1 together with stronger ordinal maximin share guarantees? For additive valuations, we prove that there always exists a complete allocation that is simultaneously EF1 and ([MATH]-out-of-[MATH])-MMS, where [MATH] is the golden ratio. For bivalued valuations, where each agent may have her own two non-negative values for the goods, we obtain a complete allocation that is simultaneously envy-free up to any good (EFX) and ([MATH]-out-of-[MATH])-MMS.
tldr: The paper proves existence of complete allocations satisfying EF1 and a golden-ratio approximation to maximin share for additive goods, with an EFX extension for bivalued valuations.
motivation: Fair division seeks allocations that are simultaneously envy-free and provide strong share guarantees, but EF1 alone only guarantees a weaker maximin-share approximation. The authors ask whether EF1 can be combined with stronger ordinal MMS guarantees.
method: The authors study additive and bivalued valuation settings and prove constructive existence results for allocations satisfying EF1 plus (phi-out-of-n)-MMS, where phi is the golden ratio, and EFX plus the same MMS guarantee for bivalued valuations.
result: For additive valuations, a complete allocation always exists that is both EF1 and (phi-out-of-n)-MMS. For bivalued valuations, a complete allocation always exists that is both EFX and (phi-out-of-n)-MMS.
conclusion: The golden ratio emerges as a tight or natural threshold for combining EF1/EFX with ordinal maximin-share guarantees, advancing fair division theory for additive and bivalued goods.

title: Your Secrets Are Showing: Deep Image Hiding Models Are Surprisingly Easy To Attack
authors: Hao Liu, Jing Yu, Weizhi Liu, Lingling Yuan, Fengyong Li, Keke Gai, Zhaoxia Yin, Xinpeng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we ask whether an attacker can go beyond detecting a hidden image and tell what it depicts, even without knowing which model hid it. We show that, for deep image hiding, this is surprisingly easy. To test this, we build an evaluation dataset of stego images generated by 11 hiding models. These models span two families (invertible neural networks and autoencoders), use different backbones (CNN, Transformer, and Mamba), and include both spatial- and frequency-domain hiding methods. We demonstrate that training HiNet [17] in the usual way yields a single decoder that can extract secret content from unseen models across these settings. Both humans and machines can recognize what it reveals. A frequency analysis shows that most models favor mid- and high-frequency embedding. Guided by this finding, we strengthen cross-model extraction by enhancing cover textures and suppressing secret textures during training. The attack extends to out-of-distribution secrets and to multi-image hiding. It even exposes private content hidden by AIRPNet [13], a recent image restoration method that uses steganography for privacy protection. What surprised us most is that decoders from every hiding model we test exhibit this ''universal'' extraction ability to varying degrees. Our code and datasets will be open-sourced.
tldr: The paper shows that a single decoder trained on one deep image-hiding model can extract hidden secret images from stego images produced by many unseen hiding models, revealing a widespread vulnerability in deep steganography.
motivation: Prior work on steganography attacks focused mainly on detecting whether a hidden image exists; the authors ask whether an attacker can also reconstruct what the hidden image depicts without knowing the embedding model.
method: They assemble an evaluation dataset of stego images from 11 hiding models (invertible neural networks and autoencoders, CNN/Transformer/Mamba backbones, spatial and frequency domain), train a HiNet-based universal decoder, and use frequency analysis to guide training by enhancing cover textures and suppressing secret textures.
result: The single decoder extracts recognizable secrets from unseen models, out-of-distribution secrets, and multi-image hiding, and even breaks privacy content hidden by AIRPNet; decoders from all tested hiding models show this universal extraction ability to varying degrees.
conclusion: Deep image-hiding models embed secrets in mid- and high-frequency bands in a model-agnostic way, making cross-model extraction surprisingly easy and undermining the security guarantees assumed by such steganographic privacy tools.

title: An Empirical Square-Root Law For The Degree Discrepancy Of Binary m-Sequences
