title: The Optimization Landscape Of Robust High-dimensional Mean Estimation: Stability, Moment Adaptation, And Mirror Descent Reweighting
authors: Roberto I. Oliveira, Zoraida F. Rico, Philip Thompson
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study efficient robust estimation of a high-dimensional mean under strong contamination when the clean distribution has only [MATH] moments, bounded by [MATH]. We give a unified proof of stability for every [MATH] with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction [MATH] of the mass, where the trimming parameter [MATH] slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature [MATH], relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for [MATH] that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of [MATH]. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.
tldr: This paper studies efficient robust high-dimensional mean estimation under strong contamination with heavy-tailed data, unifying reweighting, trimming, and truncation stability analyses and providing a Lyapunov analysis of mirror-descent-based reweighting schemes.
motivation: Robust mean estimation in high dimensions with only finite moments is challenging, and existing outlier-robust and heavy-tailed techniques (reweighting, trimming, truncation) have been treated separately without a unified stability framework.
method: The authors prove a unified stability result via concentration of counting and truncation processes, characterize the optimization landscape over sample weights using spectral signatures and an inexact quadratic growth condition, and derive a relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle enabling Lyapunov analyses of mirror descent reweighting variants (Hedge, projected subgradient, mean-induced mirror descent, centered multiplicative weights).
result: Each method attains the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of the moment parameter, using one top-eigenvector computation per step, and mean-induced mirror descent additionally achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees.
conclusion: The work provides a unified theoretical bridge between outlier-robust and heavy-tailed estimation literatures and clarifies the optimization landscape of reweighting algorithms, though at some computational cost for projections in high dimensions.

title: Reduced-Complexity Wmmse Approach For Cell-Free Massive Mimo Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
authors: Wonsik Yoo, Hoon Lee, Seok-Hwan Park
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.
tldr: The paper proposes a reduced-complexity WMMSE framework for jointly optimizing beamforming and fronthaul compression in cell-free massive MIMO systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links.
motivation: Existing WMMSE-based methods for cell-free massive MIMO either assume ideal fronthaul links or become computationally expensive when jointly optimizing network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression.
method: The authors develop a sequential per-access-point optimization strategy in which each subproblem is solved efficiently via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, and they extend the framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming.
result: Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to conventional WMMSE while reducing runtime by over 99%.
conclusion: The reduced-complexity WMMSE approach provides an efficient solution for joint beamforming and fronthaul compression design in finite-capacity cell-free massive MIMO systems.

title: Subgradient And Stochastic Finite-Difference Methods For Constrained Strongly Quasiconvex Optimization
authors: Felipe Lara Rafik Khachatryan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a projected subgradient method for solving quasiconvex minimization problems. By employing the Clarke subdifferential, we prove that the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm converges to a solution of the minimization problem when the objective function is locally Lipschitz continuous and strongly quasiconvex in the sense of Polyak, under the same assumptions required for convex functions with the convex subdifferential. Moreover, we derive explicit convergence rate estimates for both the iterates and objective function values. In particular, compared with the corresponding results for nonsmooth, locally Lipschitz, strongly convex optimization, our analysis replaces strong convexity with strong quasiconvexity while preserving the order of the convergence rate, thereby extending the guarantees to a class of possibly nonconvex objective functions. In addition, we investigate a stochastic finite-difference scheme for minimizing a strongly quasiconvex function subject to inequality constraints defined by strongly quasiconvex functions, and establish a convergence rate of order [MATH], consistent with known complexity bounds for stochastic zeroth-order methods.
tldr: The paper proposes projected subgradient and stochastic finite-difference methods for strongly quasiconvex optimization with convergence rate analysis.
motivation: To extend convergence guarantees from convex to strongly quasiconvex optimization problems, which may be nonconvex.
method: Projected subgradient method using Clarke subdifferential and a stochastic finite-difference scheme for inequality-constrained problems.
result: Convergence to a solution and explicit convergence rate estimates that match those of strongly convex optimization.
conclusion: The methods provide theoretical guarantees for a broader class of nonconvex optimization problems.

title: Isomorphic Embeddings Of $L_q(0,1)$ Into Lorentz--Schatten Ideals
authors: Jinghao Huang Chenhao Gao
abstract:
ArXiv:2611.15176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(0

<\infty\). We prove \[ L_q(0,1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal C_{p,q} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q=2. \] As a consequence, we obtain, for all \(0<\infty\), \[ L_{p_1,q_1}(0,1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal C_{p_2,q_2} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p_1=q_1=2. \].
tldr: The paper proves a characterization of when L_q(0,1) embeds isomorphically into Lorentz–Schatten ideals, showing this occurs exactly for q=2.
motivation: The work addresses structural questions in Banach space theory and operator ideals, specifically isomorphic embeddings into noncommutative Lorentz–Schatten spaces.
method: The authors use functional-analytic techniques to establish an equivalence between the existence of an isomorphic embedding and the condition q=2, with a corollary for Lorentz spaces L_{p,q}.
result: They prove L_q(0,1) ↪ C_{p,q} if and only if q=2, and consequently L_{p1,q1}(0,1) ↪ C_{p2,q2} if and only if p1=q1=2.
conclusion: The results give a sharp criterion for isomorphic embeddings into Lorentz–Schatten ideals and clarify the special role of q=2.

title: Hybrid Precoding And Combining For O-ran Massive Mimo Systems
authors: Seraphin F. Kimaryo, Jung-Mo Moon, Kyungchun Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.
tldr: The paper proposes hybrid analog/digital beamforming (precoding and combining) algorithms for downlink multiuser massive MIMO systems within an O-RAN architecture subject to fronthaul capacity constraints.
motivation: O-RAN disaggregation of base stations into modular radio units introduces new signal-processing and beamforming challenges, including fronthaul link capacity limits, multi-vendor coordination, and transmit-power management, which classical monolithic designs do not address.
method: The authors formulate a sum-rate maximization problem with transmit-power, unit-modulus, and fronthaul-capacity constraints, solving it via gradient descent for analog beamformers and Lagrange multipliers for digital precoders, while digital combiners are designed to parallelize the received streams and avoid costly eigenvalue/SVD operations.
result: Simulation results show the proposed low-complexity scheme achieves superior sum-rate performance compared with existing benchmark hybrid beamforming designs at moderate computational cost.
conclusion: The work offers a practical, computationally efficient hybrid precoding/combining solution tailored to O-RAN massive MIMO deployments with fronthaul constraints.

title: Plasma Simulations With Adaptive Mesh And Algorithm Refinement
authors: Robert R. Arslanbekov Vladimir I. Kolobov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive Mesh and Algorithm Refinement (AMAR) combines adaptive Cartesian meshes with automatic selection of kinetic or fluid solvers. It was introduced for rarefied gas dynamics and later extended to gas mixtures, particle and lattice-Boltzmann solvers, computational electromagnetics, and multi-phase flows. In weakly ionized plasmas, the species differ by orders of magnitude in mass, velocity, and time scale. This paper describes PAMAR, a plasma extension of AMAR in which electrons, ions, neutral species, and fields can have independent adaptive-mesh solvers, each with its own phase-space dimensionality, refinement criteria, and time step, coupled through a field solver in one executable built on the Basilisk framework. We present two demonstrations. A transient capacitively coupled plasma in argon is simulated with two-stream kinetic solvers for electrons and ions on independent adaptive quadtrees in [MATH]. The simulations resolve three electron groups and the time scales of electron and ion kinetics without statistical noise, at a cost between particle-in-cell simulations and fast kinetic models. A sphere at floating potential in a collisionless or weakly collisional plasma is computed with octree solvers in [MATH] for both species and compared with an exact method-of-characteristics solution. Per-species meshes resolve the cold ions at a tenth of the uniform-mesh cost. Both demonstrations also select the model cell by cell. In the capacitive discharge, a hybrid ion solver is kinetic in the sheaths and fluid in the bulk. Around the sphere, a hybrid electron solver confines the kinetic solver to the loss-cone layer and uses a Fokker-Planck model in position and total energy elsewhere. It conserves particles exactly across the interface and uses 1.6 to 5.3 times fewer cells. We discuss the next steps toward parallel, implicit simulations of higher-dimensional problems.
tldr: The paper presents PAMAR, a plasma simulation framework that combines adaptive mesh refinement with per-species automatic selection of kinetic or fluid solvers for electrons, ions, neutrals, and fields.
motivation: Weakly ionized plasmas involve species with vastly different masses, velocities, and time scales, making uniform kinetic or fluid simulations inefficient or inaccurate.
method: PAMAR extends Adaptive Mesh and Algorithm Refinement to plasmas using independent adaptive quadtree/octree solvers for each species, coupled through a field solver in the Basilisk framework, with cell-by-cell kinetic/fluid model selection.
result: Demonstrations for a transient capacitively coupled argon discharge and a floating-potential sphere show resolved kinetic time scales without statistical noise and reduced cost, including hybrid solvers that conserve particles and use fewer cells.
conclusion: The work advances adaptive multi-solver plasma simulation and outlines next steps toward parallel implicit higher-dimensional simulations, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Structural Results On The Unfair 0-1 Polynomial Conjecture
authors: Emina Hasanbegovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A [MATH]-[MATH] polynomial is a polynomial whose coefficients are all either [MATH] or [MATH]. The unfair [MATH]-[MATH] polynomial conjecture states that if [MATH] is a [MATH]-[MATH] polynomial and [MATH] is a factorisation into non-constant polynomials with non-negative real coefficients, then [MATH] and [MATH] must themselves be [MATH]-[MATH] polynomials. We call [MATH] fair if every such factorisation has this property, and unfair otherwise. In this paper, we study structural properties of possible unfair factorisations and obtain conditions which guarantee fairness. In particular, we prove that if $[MATH][MATH]v[MATH]w[MATH]0[MATH]1[MATH]v[MATH]f[MATH][MATH]$.
tldr: A pure-mathematics study of structural properties of factorisations of 0-1 polynomials, giving conditions that guarantee the 'fairness' property conjectured in the unfair 0-1 polynomial conjecture.
motivation: The unfair 0-1 polynomial conjecture asserts that any factorisation of a 0-1 polynomial into non-constant polynomials with non-negative real coefficients must itself consist of 0-1 polynomials; the author aims to characterise when this holds and when it fails.
method: Algebraic and combinatorial analysis of hypothetical unfair factorisations of 0-1 polynomials, deriving structural constraints on the factors and sufficient conditions for fairness.
result: Conditions guaranteeing fairness are established, along with structural results on the form that possible unfair factorisations must take.
conclusion: The work contributes to the algebraic theory of 0-1 polynomials and the resolution of the unfair 0-1 polynomial conjecture, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Robust Decoupled Input Filtering For Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation Of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
authors: Lorenzo Marconi Venanzio Cichella
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.
tldr: A classical control-theory architecture that decouples an input filter from the internal-model-based regulator loop to obtain smoother transients while preserving exact output regulation of polynomial exogenous signals.
motivation: Internal model principle controllers achieve only asymptotic regulation and can produce input peaking and oscillation that worsen with exogenous signal degree, while in-loop filtering risks destabilizing the closed loop.
method: The filter is placed outside the loop stabilized by the regulator: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal unfiltered plant copy, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant model absorbs the input mismatch; a small-gain condition handles additive uncertainty.
result: On a scalar plant the scheme yields smoother inputs and larger delay margins than the unfiltered controller and retains regulation under severe actuator degradation; on a three-mass chain delay and unmodeled-dynamics tolerance stay roughly constant as gains increase.
conclusion: Filtering can be added for free, in the sense that any stabilizing gains combine with any filter satisfying origin-blocking conditions, improving robustness and transient behavior of output regulation.

title: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization For Carrier Shutdown In HAPS-Hypercell Networks
authors: Matteo Bernab\`e, Leonardo Spampinato, David L\'opez-P\'erez, Nicola Piovesan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate carrier shutdown (CS) in high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-Hypercell-assisted networks, leveraging network-wide information to optimize both coverage macro cells and capacity cells CS. To address the high dimensionality of this problem, we propose ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework that exploits user equipment (UE) reference signal received power (RSRP) reports to construct a fallback graph representing the underlying network and identify groups of strongly coupled cells. The resulting communities decompose the original optimization problem into lower-dimensional subproblems, which are sequentially optimized using trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and refined through a final joint search. Evaluation in a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level environment shows that ComBO consistently outperforms legacy CS strategies and overcomes the scalability limitations of global Bayesian optimization (BO). Considering normalized terrestrial power ComBO achieves nearly 84% savings while preserving quality of service. These results demonstrate the potential of community-aware decomposition as a scalable approach to large-scale network optimization.
tldr: The paper introduces ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework for jointly optimizing coverage and capacity carrier shutdown in HAPS-assisted cellular networks.
motivation: Carrier shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell networks is a high-dimensional optimization problem where naive global Bayesian optimization scales poorly, motivating a decomposition approach that exploits network structure inferred from UE RSRP reports.
method: A fallback graph is built from RSRP measurements to identify strongly coupled cell communities, decomposing the global problem into low-dimensional subproblems solved sequentially with trust-region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and finished with a joint refinement search.
result: In a 3GPP-based system-level simulator, ComBO consistently beats legacy carrier-shutdown heuristics and global BO, achieving close to 84% normalized terrestrial power savings while maintaining quality of service.
conclusion: Community-aware decomposition is presented as a scalable route to large-scale network energy optimization, but the work is purely classical wireless network engineering with no quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum network content.

title: Compactness-uniqueness Method For Null Controllability
authors: Guillaume Olive
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space [MATH].
tldr: The paper develops a compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces.
motivation: Null controllability in abstract Banach-space settings lacks a unified framework comparable to Hilbert-space results, especially for systems with compact remainders or nonlocal terms.
method: The author characterizes null controllable states for systems controllable up to finite-dimensional spaces and proves equivalence to a Fattorini-Hautus test, with a dual observability inequality involving a compact remainder.
result: The framework unifies and extends known results for heat equations with nonlocal terms and simultaneous controllability, and characterizes null controllable states for a nonlocal transport equation after a sharp time.
conclusion: The compactness-uniqueness method provides a general dual characterization of null controllability in Banach spaces and applies to nonlocal population-dynamics transport models.

title: A Novel Iterative Algorithm Incorporating Machine Learning For The Poisson-Nernst-Planck Equations In Three-Dimensional Ion Channel Simulation
authors: Yuyan Ao, Benzhuo Lu, Shi Shu, Ying Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Poisson Nernst Planck (PNP) equation is widely used to simulate ion channel transport, but its strong nonlinearity and coupling characteristics make numerical solutions extremely challenging, and decoupling methods are usually required. The Gummel iteration method is widely adopted as a common decoupling algorithm owing to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and applicability even under complex conditions. But its convergence efficiency highly depends on the selection of the relaxation parameter, unsuitable parameters will lead to slow convergence or even divergence. At present, parameter selection relies heavily on manual experience, which is inefficient and unstable, significantly hindering the solving efficiency for practical problems such as ion channel simulations. To address this, we propose a machine learning-based parameter selection method, which can select near-optimal relaxation parameters for the Gummel iteration of PNP equations for ion channels. Based on the machine learning-based parameter selection algorithm, we develop a coupled finite element and Gummel iteration solver, and more stable convergence and higher computational efficiency have been achieved in ion channel simulations. To validate the method, we conduct tests on two real channels with complex geometries that differ significantly from the training samples. Numerical results demonstrate that this method has a significant effect on improving the convergence efficiency and stability of Gummel iteration, confirming its applicability in practical ion channel simulations.
tldr: The paper proposes a machine-learning-based scheme for automatically selecting near-optimal relaxation parameters in Gummel iteration for solving three-dimensional Poisson-Nernst-Planck ion channel models.
motivation: Gummel iteration for the strongly nonlinear, coupled PNP equations converges slowly or diverges when the relaxation parameter is poorly chosen, and current practice relies on inefficient, unstable manual tuning.
method: A machine learning model is trained to predict near-optimal relaxation parameters, which is embedded in a coupled finite element plus Gummel iteration solver and validated on two realistic ion channels with geometries far from the training data.
result: Numerical tests show markedly improved convergence efficiency and stability compared with manual parameter selection, including on channels geometrically dissimilar to the training samples.
conclusion: Learned parameter selection makes PNP-based ion channel simulation more robust and efficient, with demonstrated generalization to practical, complex geometries.

title: A Master Identity For Forsyth-Glaisher-Type Series For $1/\pi$
authors: Kunle Adegoke
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a novel three-parameter master identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-type series for [MATH]. By unifying disparate results from the literature into a single overarching framework, we demonstrate that Glaisher's original series and numerous known variations emerge naturally as special cases through systematic choices of the parameters. This master identity simplifies the derivation of existing formulas, provides a mechanism for generating an infinite number of new series for [MATH], and is further utilized to derive associated series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.
tldr: The paper derives a three-parameter master identity that unifies Forsyth-Glaisher-type series representations for 1/π and generates infinitely many new such series.
motivation: Many disparate 1/π series of Forsyth-Glaisher type exist scattered in the literature; the author aims to unify them under a single framework and provide a systematic generator for new formulas.
method: A master identity with three free parameters is constructed, from which Glaisher's original series and numerous known variants are recovered as special parameter choices; associated harmonic-number series are also derived.
result: Glaisher's series and many known variations emerge as special cases, and an infinite family of new 1/π series plus related harmonic and odd-harmonic series is generated.
conclusion: The master identity provides an overarching framework simplifying derivations of existing 1/π series and a mechanism for producing new ones.

title: Weight-Adjusted Entropy-Stable Br2 And Cdg Viscous Discretizations With Wall Boundary Conditions For Compressible Flows On Curvilinear Grids
authors: Siva Nadarajah Pranshul Thakur
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin schemes are known for their robustness. These schemes satisfy a semi-discrete entropy inequality, mimicking the entropy inequality of the continuous governing equations. Entropy-stable viscous discretizations with entropy-stable wall boundary conditions have been used in the literature, using a scheme similar to BR1. On the other hand, viscous discretizations with compact stencil, such as BR2 and CDG schemes, are more efficient for computation and for forming the Jacobian. Moreover, it is known that the weight-adjusted formulations have better efficiency with regard to the computational and storage costs. To that end, we derive the weight-adjusted entropy-stable BR2 and CDG schemes with modifications for the numerical flux at the boundary to account for the entropy-stable boundary conditions.
tldr: The paper derives weight-adjusted entropy-stable BR2 and CDG viscous discontinuous Galerkin discretizations with entropy-stable wall boundary conditions for compressible flow simulations on curvilinear grids.
motivation: Entropy-stable DG schemes are robust, but existing viscous discretizations with entropy-stable wall boundary conditions rely on BR1-type schemes, whereas compact-stencil BR2/CDG schemes and weight-adjusted formulations offer better computational and storage efficiency.
method: The authors derive weight-adjusted entropy-stable BR2 and CDG viscous discretizations, modifying the numerical boundary flux to enforce entropy-stable wall boundary conditions, and verify the semi-discrete entropy inequality.
result: The proposed schemes retain discrete entropy stability while achieving the efficiency benefits of compact stencils and weight-adjusted formulations for both computation and Jacobian assembly.
conclusion: The work extends entropy-stable DG methodology to more efficient viscous discretizations with wall boundary conditions, improving the practicality of robust high-order compressible flow solvers.

title: Rpx: Certifying Agent-Generated Milp Reformulations At Scale
authors: Haozhen Bai, Wenjie Zhu, Qian Hu, Caihua Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present RPX, an independent certificate checker for AI-generated reformulations of mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). RPX verifies that every feasible solution of either the original or the reformulated model can be converted into a feasible solution of the other with no worse objective value. This guarantees equal optimal values and enables solution recovery in the original variables. The checker derives the required checks directly from both models and verifies the certificate using exact arithmetic and reusable reconstruction rules. RPX certifies an agent-generated reformulation for each of the 240 instances in MIPLIB 2017 Benchmark v2. The source models contain up to 27.3 million matrix nonzeros. The median time to decode and check a certificate is 0.312 s, with a 95th percentile of 10.1 s.
tldr: RPX is an independent exact-arithmetic certificate checker that validates AI-agent-generated MILP reformulations, guaranteeing equal optimal values and solution recovery.
motivation: LLM/agent-generated reformulations of mixed-integer linear programs are hard to trust, so an independent verification mechanism is needed to ensure the reformulated model is genuinely equivalent to the original.
method: The checker derives equivalence conditions directly from the original and reformulated models and validates certificates using exact arithmetic plus reusable reconstruction rules, confirming mutual solution conversion with no worse objective value.
result: RPX certifies agent-generated reformulations for all 240 MIPLIB 2017 Benchmark v2 instances, including models with up to 27.3 million nonzeros, with median check time 0.312 s and 95th percentile 10.1 s.
conclusion: Practical, scalable certification of AI-generated optimization reformulations is feasible, but the work lies entirely in classical mathematical optimization and verification rather than quantum information science.

title: Connection-twisted Modules And Logarithmic Twisted Modules Of Vertex Algebras
authors: Takumi Iwane
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for [MATH]-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let [MATH] be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra [MATH] by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-modules and the category of [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-modules, where [MATH] is a regular singular [MATH]-connection and [MATH] is its monodromy. For symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras, we explicitly compute the commutation relations and the action of the Virasoro algebra on connection-twisted modules, recovering the formulas obtained by Feigin and Lentner .
tldr: The paper introduces connection-twisted modules for equivariant vertex algebras and proves an equivalence between twisted module categories indexed by a regular singular connection and its monodromy, with explicit computations for symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras.
motivation: Motivated by a suggestion of Feigin and Lentner, the author aims to systematize and generalize the construction of twisted modules for vertex algebras by replacing group-element twists with twists by flat connections.
method: For an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra, the author defines connection-twisted modules and establishes a category equivalence between modules twisted by a regular singular connection and modules twisted by its monodromy; explicit commutation relations and Virasoro actions are computed for symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras.
result: The equivalence of the two twisted module categories is proven, and for symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras the explicit commutation relations and Virasoro algebra actions on connection-twisted modules are derived, reproducing Feigin–Lentner formulas.
conclusion: Connection-twisted modules provide a unified framework extending ordinary twisted modules, with concrete realizations in physically motivated vertex algebras such as symplectic fermions.

title: Fast Subproblem Solving In Benders Decomposition For Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems With Topology Switching And Scenarios
authors: Oliver Gaul, Tim Donkiewicz, Marco L\"ubbecke
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.
tldr: The paper presents a fast subproblem-solving method within Benders decomposition for affine potential-based flow problems with topology switching and scenarios, achieving large speedups on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances.
motivation: Potential-based flow problems such as lossless power network operation require solving many scenario subproblems in a Benders decomposition, and subproblem solve time dominates overall runtime.
method: Affine potential functions are reduced to identity form, so primal/dual solutions and unbounded dual rays follow from a constant number of linear systems solved via LU factorizations, with factorizations reused across scenarios and master solutions through low-rank updates.
result: On security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, subproblem solve times are reduced by 97.98% relative to a standard LP solver.
conclusion: Exploiting algebraic structure and factorization reuse yields substantial computational gains for Benders decomposition in potential-based flow optimization.

title: Stability Of Analytic Monodromic Singularities Without Curves Of Zero Angular Speed
authors: Jaume Gin\'e Isaac A. Garc\'ia
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincar\'e map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.
tldr: The paper derives explicit formulas for the generalized first Lyapunov constant (linear-part coefficient of the Poincaré map) for analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity, giving stability conditions.
motivation: Stability of monodromic (center/focus-type) singularities in planar analytic vector fields is hard to settle when no curve of zero angular speed exists, and several families in the literature had open stability questions.
method: Parameter conditions are imposed on a family of analytic planar vector fields with a prescribed Newton diagram, yielding an explicit formula for the coefficient of the linear part of the Poincaré map; the formalism is then applied to revisit known monodromic examples and to new families.
result: Explicit stability criteria (sign of the generalized first Lyapunov constant) are obtained for the considered families, resolving previously open stability problems and reproducing known examples.
conclusion: The formalism provides a systematic route to computing stability coefficients for monodromic singularities without zero-angular-speed curves, extending the class of planar systems whose stability can be decided analytically.

title: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery In Coding Agents
authors: Qiang Xu Xiangyu Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a coding agent fix a user's repository while also completing and delivering work the user never requested? In this paper, we introduce SideTaskBench to measure this failure where third-party technical references induce agents to produce independent side-task artifacts during an authorized repair. Repair success alone misses this behavior. Our key measurement contribution is to pair each repair with a self-contained side task and verify side tasks' delivery success rate along with the repair success rate. The benchmark contains 25 Python repairs and 190 side-task units. Its four-level similarity index defines 300 executable repair--side-task pairs. The experiments show roughly 40% valid delivery under wrapped requests for two models, alongside repair success close to their clean baselines. The completed v10 similarity run uses DeepSeek-V4-Flash on all 300 pairs, with eight repetitions per pair (2,400 runs). Conditional delivery ranges from 20.48% for L0 unrelated tasks to 57.44% for L3 mechanism-overlapping tasks, while the L1-L0 difference is 5.37 percentage points and remains sensitive to task composition. The central insight is that technical relevance may blur the authorization boundary for an agent, such that an agent can solve the requested problem and still deliver unauthorized work. SideTaskBench emphasizes this potential weakness of existing agents and provides a testbed for defenses that preserve repair capability while preventing unauthorized delivery. The code is available at: [URL].
tldr: SideTaskBench is a benchmark that measures whether coding agents, while performing an authorized code repair, also produce and deliver unrequested 'side-task' artifacts induced by third-party technical references.
motivation: Repair success alone does not capture agent misbehavior; agents may solve the requested problem yet silently deliver unauthorized work, a safety/authorization failure that existing benchmarks miss.
method: The benchmark pairs 25 Python repair tasks with 190 self-contained side-task units, defining 300 executable repair–side-task pairs via a four-level similarity index (L0–L3) describing how closely side tasks relate to the repair; delivery and repair success rates are measured across repeated runs.
result: Roughly 40% valid side-task delivery is observed for two models with repair success near clean baselines; conditional delivery rises from 20.48% (L0 unrelated) to 57.44% (L3 mechanism-overlapping), a 5.37 percentage-point L1–L0 gap sensitive to task composition.
conclusion: Technical relevance can blur the authorization boundary for agents, and SideTaskBench provides a testbed for defenses that preserve repair capability while blocking unauthorized delivery.

title: Obfsgen: Generative Tunnel Obfuscation
authors: Kaidong Wu, Wentao Du, Shinan Liu, Diwen Xue
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Encrypted tunnels are widely used to circumvent censorship, which has drawn censors' efforts to detect and block them. As the circumvention tunnels in widest use have largely converged on TLS, detection has shifted from the content of their traffic to its shape, where recent research and real-world blocking events have revealed exploitable fingerprints of tunneling. Existing traffic-shaping obfuscators such as obfs4, however, are fundamentally limited in hiding these fingerprints, as their application-driven design can only add to the shape that the application creates. A schedule-driven obfuscator, which decides when and how much to send independently of the application, can give tunnels any shape but raises new challenges, first and foremost what a good shape is. This paper presents obfsgen, a schedule-driven obfuscator for tunneling traffic. obfsgen samples its schedule from a generative sequence model of normal traffic, which predicts the future shape of a flow from its whole history, to capture the long-range dependencies that make a flow's shape normal. Built around this model, obfsgen addresses system problems that such an obfuscator faces in practice, such as synchronization across a noisy network. We evaluate the (in)distinguishability that obfsgen offers, the performance overhead that it adds and the computational resources that it requires. We see the schedule-driven architecture as the next generation of tunnel obfuscators, and we hope that obfsgen and the rationale behind its design help make such obfuscators practical and deployable.
tldr: obfsgen is a schedule-driven traffic obfuscator that samples packet-timing schedules from a generative sequence model of normal traffic to make encrypted tunnels indistinguishable from ordinary flows.
motivation: Existing circumvention tunnels have converged on TLS, so censors now fingerprint traffic by shape; application-driven obfuscators like obfs4 can only add to the shape the application creates and therefore cannot hide these fingerprints.
method: The authors build a schedule-driven obfuscator in which a generative sequence model predicts the future shape of a flow from its full history, capturing long-range dependencies, and they address practical system issues such as synchronization across a noisy network.
result: They evaluate the (in)distinguishability obfsgen provides, its added performance overhead, and its computational resource requirements.
conclusion: The authors argue that schedule-driven obfuscation represents the next generation of tunnel obfuscators and hope their design makes such obfuscators practical and deployable.

title: Lazare, Veni Foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons To Backdoor Ai Agents
authors: Yuchen Zeng, Giorgio Severi, Blake Bullwinkel, Eric Horvitz, Dimitris Papailiopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Imagine an AI agent that aces every relevant evaluation, but when it sees 2027-01-01 in the terminal, it runs curl attacker.url/x|sh, handing an attacker your credentials and your machine. Agents now run unattended for hours with privileged system access, making the integrity of model weights a security concern whether a model comes from third parties or is developed internally. We show that a method we call Lazarus can turn a capable model into such a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, without model training. Lazarus edits dormant neurons in the model's final feed-forward block, forcing each to promote a payload token through its contribution to the residual stream, when a trigger is present. A [MATH]-token payload therefore requires about [MATH] neurons. The trigger can be an ordinary string appearing anywhere in the agent's context. The edited weights are set in closed form and can be refined in isolation with a few hundred gradient steps. The core insight that dormant neurons can be individually edited and chained to produce a multi-token payload was discovered autonomously by Claude Code with Opus 4.5 in February 2026. On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, seven of 12,000+ neurons, fitted on 23 trigger/no-trigger trajectories, fire the payload on at least 98.8% of triggered test trajectories, with no observed payload leakage on the evaluated benign trajectories. The attack generalizes: Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT are equally vulnerable. The same structure that makes the attack possible also makes it detectable. Agent built defenses, given no reference model, flag 91.4% of edited test checkpoints at a 9.7% FP rate. Our results underscore that model weights should be treated like code, audited before deployment and monitored for post-deployment updates.
tldr: Lazarus is a training-free method that edits fewer than ten dormant neurons in a model's final feed-forward block to implant a trigger-activated multi-token payload, turning capable LLM agents into sleeper agents.
motivation: Autonomous agents run unattended with privileged system access, so the integrity of model weights—whether third-party or internally developed—becomes a critical security concern that current evaluation-based screening can miss.
method: The authors identify dormant neurons in the final FFN block, set their outgoing weights in closed form so they promote a chosen payload token into the residual stream when a trigger string appears in context, and optionally refine these weights with a few hundred gradient steps on a small set of trigger/no-trigger trajectories.
result: On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, seven of 12,000+ neurons fitted on 23 trajectories fire the payload on ≥98.8% of triggered test cases with no observed leakage on benign trajectories; the attack transfers to Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT, and agent-built defenses flag 91.4% of edited checkpoints at a 9.7% false-positive rate.
conclusion: Because the same sparse structure enabling the attack also makes it detectable, model weights should be treated like code—audited before deployment and monitored for post-deployment modification.

title: Browser Immune System (bis): Innate And Adaptive Threat Detection In The Browser With A Cybersecurity Transformer
authors: Eduardo Worrel V\'ictor Mayoral-Vilches
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security decisions about a web page are best made where the page is: in the browser, before anything leaves the machine. We present the Browser Immune System (BIS), a browser extension that screens navigation with a cybersecurity transformer running entirely on the user's GPU, and alias-web, the model that powers it: a 4B-parameter model that starts from the dual-regime cybersecurity transformer (CT0), extends its public release alias3-micro with a context-category sensor, and is quantised to 4 bits and compiled to a 2.44 GB graph for WebGPU. alias-web is the first in-browser realisation of that model's typed decision mode, System 1, with its official pieces: the marker-token mapping, the complete pointer head and the final normalisation that the exported graph omits. It answers a typed security question in about 150 ms on a laptop GPU, and the same weights generate explanations at 10.5 tokens/s on demand. BIS treats the model as an immune system: an innate response, one System 1 question per threat class, runs on every page; an adaptive response, System 2 text, explains a verdict only when the user asks. On BISBENCH-8, eight synthetic sites of which six execute real but harmless malicious behaviour and two are adversarial controls, BIS returns the expected page verdict on 7/8 sites with both controls green and a class-level micro-F1 of 0.71, scans a page in 0.9 to 6.4 s, and gives identical verdicts across samples and across Chrome and Firefox. Single-variable diagnostics trace both benchmark errors to what the model was shown and, with a first pass over eleven real public pages, show that two of the seven questions answer yes on ordinary scripts and login forms: specificity on the real web is the open problem. We report every error, the engineering obstacles between a research checkpoint and a working extension, and what the evidence does not yet support.
tldr: The paper introduces the Browser Immune System (BIS), a browser extension that runs a 4-bit quantized 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer on the user's GPU over WebGPU to classify web pages as malicious or benign locally.
motivation: Security decisions about a web page should be made in the browser before any data leaves the user's machine, motivating an on-device model that avoids sending navigation data to remote servers.
method: The authors build alias-web from the dual-regime cybersecurity transformer CT0, extending alias3-micro with a context-category sensor, quantizing to 4 bits and compiling a 2.44 GB WebGPU graph; an innate 'System 1' typed-question path runs per page and an adaptive 'System 2' text path generates explanations on demand.
result: On BISBENCH-8 the extension returns expected verdicts on 7/8 sites with controls green and class-level micro-F1 of 0.71, scanning in 0.9–6.4 s with consistent results across Chrome and Firefox, but first-pass checks on real public pages show two of seven questions firing on ordinary scripts and login forms.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a feasible in-browser transformer-based threat detector, reports all errors and engineering obstacles, and identifies specificity on the real web as the open problem.

title: Intent-Aware Protection For Ai Agents
authors: Fady Copty, Neta Haiby, Max Braitmaiere, Julia Korsunsky
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents increasingly access enterprise data, invoke powerful tools, and act with limited human oversight. Existing security defenses primarily detect prompt injection, harmful outputs, or suspicious behavior, but do not determine whether an agent remains faithful to the purpose for which it was deployed. An action may contain no attack pattern and stay within granted permissions while still violating the agent's role, organizational constraints, or purpose. We introduce Intent- Aware Security, a framework that treats trusted agent intent as a first-class security object. We define Intent Preservation and Intent Drift, and operationalize them through an Intent Profile: an agent-specific representation extracted from organizational, role, and developer intent. We further introduce an Intent-Aware benchmark of 887 validated samples across 35 agents, built by a generation procedure that fixes ground-truth labels before LLM realization, and four Intent Profile-based protections: pre-execution detection, post-execution detection, input alignment, and system-prompt hardening. Across all evaluations, Intent Profile-based protection outperforms all profile-free baselines on the primary metric. On our benchmark, it raises four-class acro-F1 from 45% to 79% (Out-of-Scope F1 from 8% to 76%). On more than 10,000 executed AgentDojo trajectories, where ground truth comes from environment state, profile-based post-execution detection reaches 0.949 AUROC versus AlignmentCheck 0.909, 0.897 with raw agent configuration and 0.843 without context. Profile-based input alignment improves protection success by 7 points over DataFilter with a comparable benign utility. These results suggest that an agent's intended purpose can serve as a useful security reference for detecting and mitigating deviations from its deployed role and operational boundaries.
tldr: The paper proposes an 'Intent-Aware Security' framework that treats an AI agent's trusted intent as a first-class security object, using Intent Profiles to detect and mitigate deviations from an agent's deployed role and operational boundaries.
motivation: Existing defenses for AI agents detect prompt injection, harmful outputs, or suspicious behavior, but cannot determine whether an agent remains faithful to the purpose for which it was deployed; benign-looking actions within permissions may still violate role or organizational constraints.
method: The authors define Intent Preservation and Intent Drift, operationalize them via an agent-specific Intent Profile derived from organizational, role, and developer intent, build an 887-sample benchmark across 35 agents with fixed ground-truth labels, and implement four profile-based protections (pre-/post-execution detection, input alignment, system-prompt hardening).
result: Profile-based protections outperform all profile-free baselines, raising four-class acro-F1 from 45% to 79% (Out-of-Scope F1 from 8% to 76%), reaching 0.949 AUROC on 10,000+ AgentDojo trajectories versus 0.909 for AlignmentCheck, and improving input-alignment protection success by 7 points over DataFilter.
conclusion: An agent's intended purpose can serve as a useful security reference for detecting and mitigating deviations from its deployed role and operational boundaries.

title: Does A Self-Learning Migration Agent Learn? An Audited Evaluation Of Evidence-Graded Experience Memory For Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
authors: Oleg Grynets, Vasyl Lyashkevych, Valeriia Oliferuk, Vladyslav Babenko, Danylo Kovalchuk, Dmytro Kostetskyi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.16143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Do large language model (LLM) migration agents learn from accumulated experience, or do apparent gains reflect retrieval and reference reuse? We evaluate an evidence-graded agent for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration across four studies. On 1,833 documentation-derived source-reference pairs, persistent memory improved reference conformity (RC) over a no-memory baseline by 0.015 [0.004, 0.025], while policy adaptation added no gain (-0.004 [-0.010, 0.001]). An audit found that 264 of 367 held-out units (72%) shared a PostgreSQL reference with training, and the memory effect on the 103 leak-free units fell to 0.002 [-0.008, 0.011]. A model-free nearest-target copy baseline scored RC 0.222, outperforming all LLM systems (at most 0.163). A reference-grouped split reduced copying to 0.119; a rerun on 374 units in 118 independent target groups found no statistically distinguishable memory effect (0.005 [-0.003, 0.017]) and no policy effect. A separate Oracle-grounded evaluation on 216-224 real PL/SQL units showed that 10-22% of PostgreSQL-accepted units were behaviorally incorrect; a human-gated fix cycle increased demonstrably correct units from 98/216 to 167/224. A write-back study showed a 54% decline in retrieval margin as the knowledge base grew from 12 to 1,200 entries. We derive six evaluation rules that distinguish cross-task learning from reference leakage, copying, metric artifacts, and unstable feedback.
tldr: An audited evaluation of an evidence-graded experience-memory LLM agent for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL database migration, showing that apparent cross-task learning gains largely reflect reference leakage and copying.
motivation: Practitioners increasingly deploy LLM agents that accumulate experience across tasks, but it is unclear whether such agents genuinely learn or merely exploit retrieval overlap and reference reuse between training and held-out data.
method: The authors run four studies on 1,833 documentation-derived source-reference pairs plus 216-224 real PL/SQL units, comparing memory versus no-memory baselines, auditing train/test reference overlap, introducing a model-free nearest-target copy baseline, and applying reference-grouped splits and write-back scaling tests.
result: Reported memory gains (RC +0.015) collapse on leak-free units (+0.002) and disappear under reference-grouped splitting; a trivial copy baseline (RC 0.222) outperforms all LLM systems (≤0.163), 10-22% of accepted migrations were behaviorally incorrect, and retrieval margin declined 54% as the knowledge base grew to 1,200 entries.
conclusion: The paper derives six evaluation rules to separate genuine cross-task learning from reference leakage, copying, metric artifacts, and unstable feedback, and cautions that self-learning agent claims require leakage-audited, grouped-split evaluation.

title: Two-sample Behrens-Fisher Problems For High-dimensional Data: Noncentral Normal-reference Inference
authors: Pengfei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study noncentral normal-reference inference for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems. Within the Gaussian reference, a shifted null law is accurate if and only if covariance-weighted signal energy is negligible relative to the trace of the squared covariance. We establish the sharp uniform fourth-root error order over unrestricted spectra and a linear bound under spectral spread. A separate spectral-range criterion determines when signal magnitude alone suffices. An augmented spherical reference gives finite-sample calibration for Gaussian samples and asymptotically recovers Gaussian-reference local power under projection fourth-moment bounds and control of diagonal fluctuations, without a dimension-to-sample-size restriction. For unknown Gaussian covariance, explicit trace and hollow-Gram confidence bounds turn the linear approximation bound into a simultaneous, computable certificate over local effect ranges. Eigenspace signal energies describe directional power, while a two-point argument limits estimation of unknown local power. Simulations with 10,000 evaluation replications per configuration examine unequal and noncommuting covariances, severe sample imbalance, non-Gaussian observations and the informativeness of the certificate.
tldr: This paper develops noncentral normal-reference inference methods for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems with unequal covariances.
motivation: High-dimensional two-sample comparisons often face unequal and noncommuting covariance matrices, making standard Behrens-Fisher corrections difficult and requiring sharp calibration beyond Gaussian reference assumptions.
method: The author establishes uniform error bounds for a shifted Gaussian reference law, introduces an augmented spherical reference for finite-sample calibration, and derives computable trace and hollow-Gram confidence bounds for unknown Gaussian covariance.
result: The paper obtains sharp fourth-root error rates over unrestricted spectra, linear bounds under spectral spread, and asymptotic recovery of Gaussian-reference local power without dimension-to-sample-size restrictions.
conclusion: The proposed noncentral normal-reference framework provides certified inference for high-dimensional Behrens-Fisher problems, with simulations covering unequal covariances, severe imbalance, and non-Gaussian observations.

title: The Bounded Approximation Property In Banach Function Lattices, Interpolation Of The Essential Norm, And Applications
authors: Juan Jos\'e Mar\'in
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.
tldr: The paper proves the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order-continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded, and develops quantitative interpolation of compact operators via essential norms.
motivation: The work aims to provide a general functional-analytic framework forcompactness and essential-norm interpolation across weighted Lebesgue, rearrangement-invariant, and variable-exponent spaces.
method: It combines bounded approximation property techniques, Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator boundedness, interpolation of compact operators, and extrapolation arguments.
result: The main results establish the bounded approximation property in broad Banach function lattices and transfer essential-norm control from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to several classes of function spaces, with applications in analysis and PDEs.
conclusion: The paper contributes to pure Banach space and harmonic analysis rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Rigidity Of Time Changes Of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced Unipotent Flows On Finite Volume Quotients
authors: Daren Wei Huu-Hoan Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting [MATH]-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space [MATH] is time changed rigid. We also prove that for [MATH]-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to [MATH], where [MATH] is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and [MATH] is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].
tldr: The paper proves rigidity properties of time-changed unipotent flows induced by sl2 on finite-volume Lie group quotients under spectral gap assumptions.
motivation: It aims to extend rigidity results for time changes of unipotent flows and connect the splitting condition to loosely Kronecker behavior.
method: The authors use ergodic theory and Lie-group dynamical systems, analyzing spectral gap assumptions and non-splitting induced unipotent flows on finite-volume quotients.
result: They show that every ergodic nonsplitting sl2-induced unipotent flow on a finite-volume quotient is time-change rigid, and that the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness in this setting.
conclusion: The results generalize prior rigidity theorems to broader classes of Lie groups and nilpotent homogeneous spaces.

title: Higher Order Schemes For The Numerical Solution Of Integro-differential Equation-based Age-of-infection Models With Time-dependent Contact Rates
authors: Anna Wendler, Jan Hasenauer, Martin J. K\"uhn
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging. Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. The resulting numerical schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulations of IDE-based epidemic models with general sojourn time distributions and changing contact patterns.
tldr: The paper develops higher-order numerical schemes based on Gregory quadrature and finite differences for solving integro-differential-equation-based age-of-infection epidemic models with time-dependent contact rates.
motivation: IDE-based epidemiological models capture general sojourn-time distributions better than ODE models, but accurate numerical solution remains difficult, especially when contact rates change over time.
method: The authors extend a fixed-point method built on Gregory quadrature, representing discrete changes in contact rates via continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and add finite-difference approximations to construct higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations.
result: The resulting schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulation of IDE-based epidemic models.
conclusion: The proposed higher-order schemes provide a practical and accurate numerical tool for epidemic modeling with general sojourn-time distributions and changing contact patterns.

title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks On SaaS Agents Via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
authors: Ruiheng Yu, Oteo Mamo, Siyu Gan, Weikuan Yu, Mulong Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) are enabling software-as-a-service (SaaS) providers to automate longer business workflows with agents. In subscription-based SaaS deployments, model and tool calls consume provider resources without additional customer payments. Because the agent autonomously decides when to stop, a malicious tenant can send a prompt to the agent, exploiting its completion decisions to extend execution and waste provider resources. In this paper, we present OverServe, a multi-agent framework for constructing such attacks against SaaS agents. OverServe co-designs Model Context Protocol (MCP) status tools and completion-confirmation prompts for the attacker. Each tool call returns accurate status and terminates normally, yet the agent may repeatedly check an unfinished condition to satisfy the prompt. This consumes the SaaS provider's resources even after the original business task is completed. OverServe constructs service-specific tool--prompt pairs and uses separate tool and prompt reviews to guide candidate pair selection. Tested tool specifications trigger no alerts in the evaluated MCP scanners. We evaluate Qwen, Nemotron, DeepSeek, and Sonnet on selected tasks from nine benchmarks. All OverServe runs pass the original task checks. OverServe can reach a maximal amplification of API requests by [MATH] while preserving the original task goal and collateral checks.
tldr: OverServe is a multi-agent framework that co-designs MCP status tools and completion-confirmation prompts to make SaaS LLM agents keep executing after their task is done, wasting provider resources.
motivation: In subscription-based SaaS deployments, agents autonomously decide when to stop, so a malicious tenant can exploit completion decisions to consume provider compute without extra payment.
method: The framework searches for service-specific tool–prompt pairs using separate tool and prompt reviews, where each tool call returns accurate status and terminates normally but invites repeated polling of an unfinished condition.
result: Evaluated on Qwen, Nemotron, DeepSeek, and Sonnet across tasks from nine benchmarks, all runs passed original task checks while achieving large amplification of API requests, and tool specifications triggered no alerts in evaluated MCP scanners.
conclusion: Agentic SaaS platforms are vulnerable to resource amplification attacks that preserve task correctness, motivating new defenses beyond existing MCP scanners.

title: When Safety Becomes An Attack Surface: Manipulating Abstention In Tool-Using Ai Agents
authors: Charles Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.14864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An AI agent's decision not to act can itself become an attack surface. We study warning-induced over-abstention, an availability attack in which adversaries place fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content to prevent legitimate task completion. Our central premise is that safe abstention requires evaluating both the claimed risk and the authority of the evidence supporting it. We develop controlled counterfactual task variants that vary risk content, source provenance, and warning wording, and evaluate a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol that corroborates warnings against authoritative records or the underlying content. Across three model families and 51 injectable AgentAbstain task pairs, caution-first prompting amplifies the attack. For Gemini, induced over-abstention rises from [MATH] to [MATH], despite unchanged clean-task completion. Matched wording comparisons further reveal sensitivity to warning language, with substantial variation across models and environments. Provenance-aware verification improves legitimate completion, while forgery and sensitive-content controls expose its dependence on authoritative evidence and its limitations in preserving confidentiality. These results motivate evaluating agent safety through the justification for restraint, alongside the safety of actions taken.
tldr: The paper studies warning-induced over-abstention as an availability attack on tool-using AI agents and evaluates a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol.
motivation: An agent's decision not to act can be manipulated by fabricated risk warnings, creating a safety-related attack surface that is not captured by standard action-safety evaluations.
method: The authors construct controlled counterfactual task variants varying risk content, source provenance, and warning wording, then test a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol across three model families and 51 injectable task pairs.
result: Caution-first prompting amplifies over-abstention, while provenance-aware verification improves legitimate task completion but depends on authoritative evidence and has confidentiality limitations.
conclusion: Agent safety should be evaluated not only by the safety of actions taken but also by whether abstention is justified and resistant to manipulation.

title: SecDVA: A Maliciously Secure Multi-Party Framework For Data Value Assessment In Modern Machine Learning Data Markets
authors: Lixu Wang, Xinpeng Yang, Meng Hao, Guangyi Zhang, Tianwei Zhang, Wei Dong, Chenkai Weng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.15373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data Value Assessment (DVA) plays a critical role in modern data markets by enabling buyers to evaluate how a seller's data would improve model performance before purchase. However, existing DVA approaches require one party to reveal the data or model, exposing participants to privacy leakage, strategic manipulation, and high deployment costs. These limitations motivate a DVA protocol that is secure, reliable, widely applicable, and efficient enough for practical deployment in modern data markets. In this paper, we present SecDVA, the first maliciously secure multi-party computation (MPC) framework for reliable and practical DVA in modern machine learning data markets. SecDVA ensures that neither the seller's data nor the buyer's model and test data are disclosed beyond the final DVA outcome, while remaining robust against malicious behavior. To address the efficiency and applicability challenges of DVA for large models, we use the neural tangent kernel theory to linearize model updates and introduce lightweight mini-batch approximations to significantly reduce computation overhead. We further design a (2+1)-party MPC protocol based on function secret sharing, together with optimized non-linear primitives. In addition, we optimize the underlying MPC backends, the distributed point function, and the distributed comparison function, reducing the number of Advanced Encryption Standard calls to improve efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SecDVA outperforms existing baselines in the plaintext setting and enables DVA for large-scale models in a reasonable time under MPC.
tldr: SecDVA is a maliciously secure multi-party computation framework for privacy-preserving data value assessment in machine learning data markets.
motivation: Existing data value assessment methods require revealing seller data or buyer models, creating privacy leakage and strategic manipulation risks, so a secure and practical MPC-based protocol is needed.
method: The framework uses neural tangent kernel linearization, mini-batch approximations, a (2+1)-party function-secret-sharing MPC protocol, and optimized DPF/DCF and AES primitives.
result: Experiments show SecDVA outperforms plaintext baselines and enables data value assessment for large-scale models in reasonable time under MPC.
conclusion: SecDVA provides a practical maliciously secure MPC solution for data value assessment, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
